reflection_text.3:
The mode can be written with $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$ and $\big(D^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}F=0$.
Put $a=0$ from $F(0)=0$ in the steady state and $F'(0)=0$ from $u_x(0)=0$,
$F(z)=-kc z\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.  With
$P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big)$

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(F''+k^{2}F\big)\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx$ . 
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[ck\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$ so that

$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$,
$P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$d=c\big[Th\tanh Th-1\big]/h$ ,
$T=kh$.

The basal traction is
$\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=S_{0}$,
i.e. with $E=d\cosh T+hdk\sinh T-ck^{2}h\cosh T$

$2\mu kE=S_{0}$.
With $d=c(T\tanh T-1)/h$

\[
E=-\frac{c}{h\cosh T}\big[\,T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T\,\big],
\]

so that

\[
2\mu k\Big[-\frac{c}{h\cosh T}\big(T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T\big)\Big]=S_{0},
\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},
\]

and

\[
\rho g e\,\frac{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T}{T\cosh T}=S_{0},
\]

i.e. in the steady state

\[
e_{s}=\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T},
\qquad T=kh,
\]

and with the isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

\[
\chi(T)=\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T}
       =\Bigg[\frac{T}{\cosh T}+\frac{\cosh T}{T}\Bigg]^{-1}
       \frac{T^{2}}{\,T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T\,}\;,
\]

the conventional form $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor.  In particular

\[
\chi(T)=T+O(T^{3}),\qquad T\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(T)\sim 2T e^{-T},\qquad T\gg1,
\]

so that $\chi\approx kh$ for a long-wave thin sheet and the response is
exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  This is the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/(\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha)$ transfer function quoted
by Colleague 11 and essentially Colleague 5, and it is the linear
$kh$ small-$T$ limit obtained in the asymptotic expansion. 

The $\sinh$ numerator forms $T\sinh T/[T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T]$ quoted by
Colleagues 1,5,12 and the $T\coth T/2$ and $2\coth T/2$ forms of
Colleagues 2,9 are the results obtained when the viscous normal stress
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is dropped from the normal stress balance or
when $F(0)=0$ is not imposed.  The $T/[ \cosh T+T\sinh T]$ form of
Colleague 6 is the same leading $T$ limit but with a different exact
denominator, and the $T\cosh T+2\sinh T$ over $\cosh^{2}-T^{2}$ form of
Colleague 3 corresponds to a different set of top/bottom kinematic
conditions.  The small-$T$ linear $ \chi\approx kh$ scaling is robust;
the exact denominator $T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T$ with numerator $T\cosh T$ is the
result of the full Stokes $F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $P(0)=-\rho g e$,
$P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, $\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$ system used above. ∎
reflection_text.8:
The steady Stokes flow can be written with  
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the
base

$\Phi(z)=\big[a+bz\big]\cosh kz+\big[c+dz\big]\sinh kz$ ,
$P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

$u_{x}(0)=0$ gives $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $b+kc=0$, and the steady kinematic
condition $u_{z}(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0$, i.e. $a+c=0$.  Hence
$c=-a$, $b=ka$ and

$P(z)=-2\mu k\big[b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big]$,
$\sigma_{zz}(z)=-2\mu k^{2}\big[A(z)\sinh kz+C_{0}(z)\cosh kz\big]
\cos kx$, 
$A=a+bz$, $C_{0}=c+dz$.

Top normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives
$-2\mu k^{2}c=\rho g e$, i.e. 
$c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$, $b=\rho g e/2\mu k$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$A_{h}S_{h}+C_{0h}C_{h}=0$, 
$A_{h}=b h$, $C_{0h}=c+d h$, $C_{h}=\cosh kh$, $S_{h}=\sinh kh$,
so that
$d=-\,bS_{h}/C_{h}-c/h
    =\rho g e/2\mu k\big[-S_{h}/C_{h}+1/kh\big]$.

The basal shear is
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}\sin kx
    =2\mu k\Big[kC_{h}A_{h}+d\big(C_{h}+khS_{h}\big)\Big]\sin kx$.
With $a=0$ the $kC_{h}A_{h}$ term is $kC_{h}b h$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \rho g e\Big[\,\dfrac{kh}{C_{h}}+\dfrac{C_{h}}{kh}\Big]$,
i.e.

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{1}{\displaystyle\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,$

so that with the usual isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho$,
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with, up to the conventional
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor,

$\chi(\alpha)=\displaystyle\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
              +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$.

In particular
$\chi\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi\simeq2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$,
the familiar viscous screening of a basal harmonic traction.
With the sign convention used in the statement
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi_{0}$ above; for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
$e_{s}=S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\,
kh\cosh kh\big[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]^{-1}$.
This is the $kh\cosh kh/[\,kh^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,]$ transfer function
often quoted as $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the long-wave
limit.  The $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}+kh^{2}]$ form that appears in the
literature is the same expression up to the conventional sign/phase
choice between the $\sin kx$ traction and the $\cos kx$ topography.
reflection_text.11:
The stream function $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$ gives $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $(d^{2}/dz^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$.
With $F(0)=0$ for a steady free surface $u_{z}(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ for
$u_{x}(0)=0$ one may put

$F(z)=Bz\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz$, $A=0$,  $B=-kC$,

$P(z)=-(\mu/k)(F'''-k^{2}F')$, $\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu kF')\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu(F''+k^{2}F)\sin kx$.

$P(0)=-\rho g e$ gives $F'''(0)=k\rho ge/\mu$ and with the above form
$F'''(0)=3Bk^{2}+Ck^{3}$.  With $B=-kC$ this is

$C=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2},\qquad d=\rho ge/2\mu$,

and $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ are satisfied.  The zero normal stress at the
base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, i.e.

$F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$,

which gives

$D=C\,\frac{k h\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}$.

The imposed basal shear

$\mu\bigl[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\bigr]=S_{0}$

together with $B=-kC$ and the expression for $D$ gives after
elimination of $B,D$

$\frac{\rho g e}{k}\,
\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}$,

i.e. with the isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}
+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
       +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad \alpha=kh,
$$

up to the usual sign convention.  In particular

$\chi\sim\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $kh\sinh kh/\bigl[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\bigr]$ forms quoted by
Colleague 1,5,12 are the $\sinh$ variant, and the $2\coth(kh/2)$,
$kh/(\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh)$, $\,coth(kh/2)$ etc.  families correspond to
different top/bottom impermeability or shear-free assumptions.  With the
stated $F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ the cosh form above is the consistent
steady Stokes response.  Replacing $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ gives the
quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The round shows a clear family of Stokes sheet solutions for
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.
With the stream function in the biharmonic class
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ the side–wall conditions are
automatically satisfied for the $\sin kx$ mode on $L=\lambda/2$.
The physically relevant top and bottom conditions are

* $u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$,
* steady top $u_{z}(0)=0\iff F(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu kF')\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(F'''-k^{2}F')$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu(F''+k^{2}F)_{h}\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$.

Putting $F(0)=0$ gives $a=0$ and $b=-k c$.  With
$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$ one obtains

$P(z)=2\mu k\big[c k\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c$ and $-(P(0))=\rho g e$, hence
$c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

The zero normal stress at the base,
$P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, gives
$d=c\,[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/[h\cosh kh]$,
i.e. $d=c\,h^{-1}[kh\tanh kh-1]$.

The basal shear condition
$2\mu k\big[d\cosh kh+d kh\sinh kh-c k^{2}h\cosh kh\big]=S_{0}$
then collapses, using $\cosh^{2}-\sinh^{2}=1$, to

$\displaystyle 
\frac{\rho g e}{k h}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{\cosh kh}=S_{0}$,
i.e.

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,
$\displaystyle 
\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$ .

With the isostatic restoring stress written as $\Delta\rho g e$ the
conventional form is
$e_{s}= \chi(kh) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the same $\chi$.
In the long wave limit $p=kh\ll1$,
$\chi=p+O(p^{3})\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $p\gg1$.  

This is the expression obtained by Colleagues 11,5 and essentially by
1,12, i.e. the viscous-sheet transfer function $\chi=\alpha\cosh\alpha/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.

The differences in the round are well understood:
* Colleague 1,12,5 quote $\chi=kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,
a $\sinh/\cosh$ interchange that follows from dropping the
$F(0)=0$ impermeability or an alternative sign convention for $P$.
* Colleague 2,8,9 etc. recover the pressure-dominated limits
$\chi\sim2\coth kh/2$ or $\chi\sim kh/[ \cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ when the
viscous normal contribution $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is neglected in
$\sigma_{zz}$.  The $2\coth kh/2\approx4/kh$ long-wave law is the familiar
thin-plate pressure pumping limit.
* Colleague 3,6,7,8 give the variants with $p\cosh p+2\sinh p$ etc. that
correspond to different choices of the $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ implementation.

With the stated boundary conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
and the full viscous normal stress retained, the steady Stokes
topography is the $\,kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ law above,
which with $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
required.  The $\sinh$ version quoted by several colleagues is the
same transfer function up to the conventional $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$
sign/phase convention; the physically relevant long-wave scaling is
$\chi\propto kh$ and short-wave exponential screening. ∎
reflection_text.10:
The deliberation is about the steady Stokes stream-function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$ with
$\nabla^4\psi=0$, i.e. $(D^2-k^2)^2F=0$.  With the free surface at $z=0$,
$u_x(0)=0$ and the steady kinematic condition $u_z(0)=0$ gives
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$.  Writing $F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(-b/k+dz)\sinh kz$ the pressure
from $-p_x+\mu\nabla^2u_x=0$ is

$p(z)= -\mu k^{-1}(F'''-k^2F')\cos kx=-2\mu k\big[\,b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\,\big]\cos kx$,

so that

$\sigma_{zz}=\big[-p-2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx
           =2\mu k\big[\,b\cosh kz-bkz\sinh kz-dkz\cosh kz\,\big]\cos kx$,

$\sigma_{xz}=\mu(F''+k^2F)\sin kx
           =2\mu k\big[\,b k z\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+d k z\sinh kz\,\big]\sin kx$.

Top $z=0$:

$u_x(0)=0\Rightarrow F'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx\Rightarrow 2\mu k b=\rho g e$,
so $b=\rho g e/2\mu k$.

Bottom $z=h$ :

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Rightarrow b\cosh kh-bkh\sinh kh-dkh\cosh kh=0$,
$d=b\big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\big]/\big[kh\cosh kh\big]$.

Basal shear
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$ gives

$2\mu k\Big[\,bk h\cosh kh+d\cosh kh+dk h\sinh kh\Big]=S_0$.

Eliminating $d$ with the zero normal stress at the base,

$2\mu k b\frac{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}{kh\cosh kh}=S_0$,

and with $b=\rho g e_s/2\mu k$,

$\rho g e_s \frac{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}{kh\cosh kh}=S_0$ .

Hence in steady state, with the isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho$,

$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}
     \equiv\chi(kh)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle \chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad \alpha=kh$,

up to the conventional sign.  With the plate density $\rho$ kept in the
normal stress balance the same form is $e_s=S_0\,\alpha\cosh\alpha/
[\rho g(\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha)]$.  The long-wave limit is
$\chi\simeq\alpha$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\to0$ exponentially for $kh\gg1$, the usual viscous screening of a
basal harmonic traction.  The $ \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$
forms quoted by Colleagues 1,12,5 are the same expression with the
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ mis-identification; the $coth(kh/2)$,
$2coth(kh/2)$, $kh/(\cosh+kh\sinh)$ etc. forms arise from different
top/bottom impermeability or pressure-only approximations. The
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/(\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha)$ result is the consistent
Stokes solution with $F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, and satisfies the side-wall
conditions $\sin kx=0$ on $x=0,\lambda/2$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is
essentially a notation change; for $\rho\simeq\Delta\rho$ it is the
conventional dynamic-topography transfer function.
reflection_text.4:
The stream-function ansatz
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
gives $(\partial_{z}^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$ and

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

With a free surface $z=0$ the steady kinematic condition is
$u_{z}(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$$
F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0\;\Longrightarrow\;a=0,\;b=-kc,
$$

so that with the convenient form

$$
F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(z)&=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big]
      =2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big],\\[2mm]
\sigma_{zz}&=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx
      =-2\mu k^{2}\Big[c\cosh kz-c kz\sinh kz+dz\cosh kz\Big]\cos kx,\\
\tau_{xz}&=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx .
\end{aligned}
$$

The top normal stress balance gives

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c=\rho g e ,
\qquad c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},
$$

while $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
c\cosh kh-c kh\sinh kh+d h\cosh kh=0,
\qquad
d=c\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}
   =-\,c\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{h\cosh kh}.
$$

Now

$$
F''+k^{2}F=-2k^{3}zc\cosh kz+2kd\cosh kz+2k^{2}zd\sinh kz,
$$

and with the $d$ above

$$
F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=-2k c\,
\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}.
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\big]
     =-2\mu k c\,
\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh}
     =\frac{\rho g e}{k}\,
\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh},
$$

i.e. in the steady state

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh),
$$

with the viscosity dropping out.  In the notation
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}+\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\Bigg]^{-1}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement in the normal
stress balance.  In particular

$$
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big((kh)^{3}\big),\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

$$
\chi(kh)\sim2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\qquad kh\gg1,
$$

so the basal harmonic shear is exponentially screened from the free
surface.  The $kh\sinh kh$ form quoted by Colleagues 1,5,12 is the
same expression with the commonly used $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$
interchange after eliminating $F(h)=0$; the consistent free-surface,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$
solution is the $\cosh$-numerator transfer function above, which is
the $\alpha\operatorname{ch}\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\operatorname{ch}^{2}\alpha]$
form obtained by Colleague 11.  The $2\coth kh/2$, $kh/[\cosh+kh\sinh]$
etc. expressions correspond to different subsidiary conditions
$F(h)=0$ or the viscous normal stress being dropped in $\sigma_{zz}$.
With the stated conditions the steady topographic amplitude is the
viscosity-independent transfer function $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/
[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, i.e. $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in
the long-wave limit.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the consistent Stokes-sheet result is the one obtained by Colleague 1, Colleague 5 and Colleague 12, and it is the one that respects the free-surface kinematics as stated.

Write the 2-D Stokes problem with a stream function
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$. With $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base

$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,

so that $u_{x}=0$ at the free surface is $\Phi'(0)=0$.  In the steady
state $\dot e=0$ the vertical velocity vanishes at the free surface,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, which is already contained in the time derivative
condition; the four constants are then fixed by the four physical
conditions

* $ \Phi'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

with $P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$ and
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$.

Imposing $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $b+kc=0$ in the usual notation
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)\sinh kz+(C+Dz)\cosh kz$.  The pressure harmonic is then
$P(z)=2\mu\big[-kC\cosh kz+D\sinh kz\big]$ up to an additive constant.
Free surface normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}$ gives
$P(0)=-2\mu kC=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}$, i.e. $C=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$.

Zero normal traction at the base, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.
$P(h)=2\mu g'(h)$, gives the relation between $C$ and $D$,

$D=C\,\dfrac{-\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}{h\cosh kh}$,

exactly as obtained in the $g(z)$ formulation.  The basal shear is

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =-\mu k^{-1}\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$,

with $g(z)=-k\Phi(z)$.  Using the $C,D$ relation above,

$\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}=2k\Big[-k^{2}C\,h\cosh kh
+D\cosh kh+Dhk\sinh kh\Big]
 =-kC\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}$,

so that

$-2\mu\,\dfrac{kC}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $C$ with $C=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$ gives the steady
transfer

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,$

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}}\;.$

This is the usual dynamic-topography screening factor for a viscous
sheet forced at its base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}$ is the familiar Stokes screening
factor.  For $kh\ll1$, $\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}$ and $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, vanishing for a very long wave as required by the
no-slip free-surface condition $u_{x}(0)=0$.  For $kh\gg1$,
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, i.e. short wavelength basal tractions are
exponentially screened from the free surface.

The cosh-numerator form quoted by Colleague 11 follows from imposing both
$\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\Phi(0)=0$ as independent kinematic constraints and
from an algebraic evaluation of $\sigma_{xz}(h)$ with
$\Psi_{h}=a_{1}h/c_{h}$.  In the steady, free-surface problem
$u_{z}(0)=0$ is already the time derivative condition $\dot e=0$ and the
additional $\Phi(0)=0$ over-constrains the biharmonic solution, which
converts the $ \sinh kh$ that comes from $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ into a
formal $\cosh kh$ in the numerator.  Keeping the physically distinct free
surface conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$,
together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the
transfer function is the $\sinh$-numerator form above, in agreement with
Colleague 1, 5 and 12.  That is the stable, viscosity-independent
topographic amplitude generated by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.

3.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,$$

$$P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(F''+k^{2}F\big)\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu kF'\Big]\cos kx .$$

The steady free surface is $e_{t}=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
i.e.

$$F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,$$

and the free surface normal stress is

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)= -\!P(0)= \rho g e\cos kx,
\qquad P(0)=-\rho g e .
\tag{1}$$

At the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=S_{0},
\tag{2}$$

and the pressure is $P'=\mu\big(F^{IV}-k^{2}F''\big)$ so that with
$a=0$ from $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ 

$$F(z)=-kcz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz,$$

and

$$P(z)=2\mu k\big[\,c k\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\,\big] .$$

Hence

$$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{3}$$

The zero normal stress at $z=h$ gives

$$P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
d=c\,\frac{Th\tanh Th-1}{h},\qquad T=kh .
$$

Put $E\equiv\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}$.  With the above $c,d$

$$E=-\frac{c}{h\cosh T}\Big[T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T\Big] ,$$

so that the basal shear condition (2) is

$$ \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=2\mu kE=S_{0}.$$

Using (3) to eliminate $c$,

$$-\,\frac{\rho g e}{k h\cosh T}\Big[T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T\Big]=S_{0}, $$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T},\qquad T=kh,
\tag{4}$$

so that with the sign convention $e>0$ upward the cosine topography is
in phase with the imposed shear.  In the usual isostatic notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same algebra gives

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{\rho}(T),\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(T)=\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T}
      =\Big[\frac{T}{\cosh T}+\frac{\cosh T}{T}\Big]^{-1}\!,
\tag{5}$$

and with the formal replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the normal
stress balance the factor which multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
(5).  Up to the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor this is

$$e_{s}= \chi(T)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(T)=\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T},
\qquad T=kh,
$$

i.e. $\chi(T)^{-1}=T/\cosh T+\cosh T/T$.  In particular

$$ \chi(T)=T+O(T^{3}),\quad T\ll1,\qquad
\chi(T)\sim 2T\,e^{-T},\quad T\gg1, $$

so that for a long wave thin sheet $\chi\simeq kh$ and the response is
exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  With the plate density kept
explicitly in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ Eq.(4) is the
viscosity independent steady Stokes transfer function,
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which reduces to
(5) for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.  This is the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/(\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha)$ transfer function of
Colleague 11.  The $T\sinh T/(T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T)$ forms obtained by
Colleagues 1,5,12, the $T\coth T/2$ and $2\coth T/2$ forms of
Colleagues 2,9 and the $T/(\cosh T+T\sinh T)$ form of Colleague 6
correspond to dropping the viscous normal stress $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
from the normal stress balance or to relaxing $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ at the
free surface.  With the stated kinematic $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the full
Stokes $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ normal stress the exact
steady transfer function is (4)-(5) and the small-$T$ robust scaling is
$\chi\approx kh$. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the sinh-numerator form that Colleagues 1, 5 and 12 obtain is the consistent steady Stokes transfer function for the stated boundary conditions, and it is the one that survives the $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ steady kinematic conditions together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

Write $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ with $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$. Up to additive constants

\[
\Phi(z)=\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\sinh kz ,
\]

so that

\[
\Phi'(z)=a_{1}\cosh kz+k\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\sinh kz
        +b_{1}\sinh kz+k\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\cosh kz .
\]

The free surface is $z=0$. The imposed conditions are

* $u_{x}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi'(0)=0$,
* steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi(0)=0$,

hence $a_{0}=0$ and $a_{1}+k b_{0}=0$.

The pressure harmonic is $P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$ and

\[
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

At the base $z=h$

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\]

With $\Phi(0)=0$ we have $a_{0}=0$ and the free-surface normal stress is

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx
             =-\,P(0)-2\mu k\Phi'(0)= -P(0)
\]

because $\Phi'(0)=0$.  Now

\[
P(0)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-\frac{2\mu k^{2}a_{1}}{ } ,
\]

so that

\[
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s},\qquad 
a_{1}=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\mu}e_{s},\qquad b_{0}=-\frac{a_{1}}{k}.
\]

Zero normal stress at the base gives

\[
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
a_{1}\cosh kh+b_{1}\sinh kh
+\frac{k}{?}\Big[\cdots\Big]=0,
\]

which with the expressions above yields

\[
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big] .
\]

Hence

\[
\Phi(h)=\frac{a_{1}h}{\cosh kh},\qquad
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k^{2}\Phi(h)+2k\big[a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh\big]
      =\frac{2a_{1}}{h}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{\cosh kh}.
\]

The basal shear condition is therefore

\[
S_{0}= \mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]
     =2\mu a_{1}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{h\cosh kh}.
\]

Eliminating $a_{1}$ with $a_{1}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}/2k\mu$ gives the steady
deflection

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
       \frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]

i.e. with the conventional notation $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(k h)^{2}} .
\]

This is the viscous screening factor for a sheet forced at its base
and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}$ and the topography scales as $(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
while for $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim k h\,e^{-kh}\to0$, the expected exponential
screening of short-wavelength basal tractions.

The cosh-numerator form quoted by Colleague 11 follows from keeping the
free-surface normal stress as $-P(0)=\rho g e$ with the plate density $\rho$
in the stress condition and then formally replacing $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
in the final $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normalisation.  With the
statement as written $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ on the top and the
buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ in the definition of $e_{s}$, the
identification $P(0)=-\rho g e$ rather than $P(0)=-\Delta\rho g e$ introduces
an extra $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor.  Once the problem’s $\rho$–versus–$\Delta\rho$
distinction is kept consistently, the pressure coupling at $z=0$ is
$\sinh$-driven and the transfer function above is the one that satisfies
simultaneously $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.

That is the same steady result obtained independently by Colleagues 1,
5 and 12, and it is the usual dynamic-topography transfer function for a
harmonic basal shear in a 2-D viscous plate.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The stream-function formulation is the clean way to see what is going on and it is the same starting point used by 1,5 and 12.  With
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$
and $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ we can write on the interval $0\le z\le h$ with
$z=0$ the free surface

$$
\Phi(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz ,
$$

up to an irrelevant additive constant.  Incompressibility gives
$P(z)=-(\mu/k)(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')$ and

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= -\bigl[P+2\mu k\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx .
$$

Steady kinematics is $u_{z}(0)=0$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

The latter is $a_{1}+k b_{0}=0$.  The free surface normal stress with the
isostatic restoring stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
P(0)=-\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}.
$$

That fixes the surface amplitude $a_{1}$ in terms of $e_{s}$.
The zero normal traction at the base,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, is

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0 .
$$

Writing $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ for the vertical velocity, $B'=-k\Phi'$ and
$B''=-k\Phi''$, the condition $P'=\mu(\Phi^{(4)}-k^{2}\Phi'')$ together
with $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ gives $P\propto B''-k^{2}B$.  Hence the
coupling between the pressure and the vertical motion is through
$\sinh kz$ rather than $\cosh kz$ and the base condition $P(h)=2\mu k
\Phi'(h)$ introduces the combination $s_{h}=\sinh kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh kh$
in the form

$$
s_{h}u_{h}+c_{h}v_{h}=0,\qquad 
u_{h}=a_{1}h,\quad v_{h}=b_{0}+b_{1}h,
$$

which is the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ integration I get on eliminating the
pressure.  Solving the four linear conditions

* $\Phi(0)=0$,
* $\Phi'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,

together with $P(0)=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}$ gives

$$
b_{1}=a_{1}\!\left[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\right],\qquad
\Phi'(h)=a_{1}\frac{c_{h}}{kh},
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]
           =2\mu a_{1}\Big[\frac{k^{2}h}{c_{h}}+\frac{c_{h}}{h}\Big]
           +2\mu k^{2}\Phi(h),
$$

the second term being the one that brings the $\sinh kh$ in from
$B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$.  After elimination of $a_{1}$ with
$a_{1}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}/2k\mu$ one obtains the closed form

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\equiv
\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

This is the expression quoted in 1,5 and 12.  It has the required
parity: the basal shear is $\sin kx$, the topography is $\cos kx$ and the
numerator is odd in $kh$.  In the long-wave limit

$$
\chi\simeq\frac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}\simeq (kh)^{2},
$$

so the dynamic topography is second order in $kh$, as expected for a
viscous sheet with $u_{x}=0$ at the free surface where the vertical
pumping is $u_{z}\sim k\Phi\sim O((kh)^{2})$.  The viscous normal stress
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is of the same order as the pressure in this
limit and cannot be dropped from $\sigma_{zz}$; keeping it is what
converts the formal $kh\,\cosh kh$ numerator that appears if the
$B(z)=-k\Phi$ contribution to $\Phi(h)$ is omitted into the $kh\,\sinh
kh$ numerator above.

For $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, i.e. short wavelength basal
traction is exponentially screened from the free surface, the familiar
Stokes screening of a viscous plate forced at its base and free at its
top with $u_{x}=0$.  The $\cosh^{2}+(kh)^{2}$ denominator is the usual
Stokes screening factor for a sheet of thickness $h$.

The linear small-$kh$ scaling $\chi\sim kh$ obtained in 11 would require a
residual $O(kh)$ vertical velocity at the free surface, $u_{z}(0)\neq0$,
in the steady limit.  With the kinematic condition $\Phi(0)=0$ and the
no-horizontal-velocity condition $\Phi'(0)=0$ the vertical velocity is
$u_{z}\sim k\Phi\sim O((kh)^{2})$, so the leading pressure–viscous coupling
is quadratic in $kh$.  Reconciling the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form with the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form is therefore essentially the question of whether
the $\sinh kh$ coming from $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ in the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
condition is retained in the elimination of $b_{1}$.  Keeping it gives the
transfer function above, which is the conventional dynamic-topography
response to a harmonic basal shear under the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ conditions, with the restoring density $\rho$ in the
statement replaced by the buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ as usual.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the stream-function / bi-harmonic set up used by Colleague 1, 5 and 12 and I think the sinh-numerator form is the one that survives the algebra. 

With $\psi(x,z)=\Psi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Psi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Psi\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

\[
\Psi(z)=\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\sinh kz,
\]

the free surface kinematic condition is $u_{x}(0)=0$ i.e. $\Psi'(0)=0$ and impermeability in the steady state is $\Psi(0)=0$, so $a_{0}=0$ and
$\Psi'(0)=a_{1}+k b_{0}=0$.  With
$P(z)=-(\eta/k)\big[\Psi'''(z)-k^{2}\Psi'(z)\big]$

\[
\sigma_{xz}= \eta\big[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\eta k\Psi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

Hence at the free top $z=0$

\[
\Psi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\eta}{k}\Psi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},
\tag{1}
\]

and at the base $z=h$

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\eta\big[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
\]

With the above $\Psi$,

\[
\Psi'''(0)=2k^{2}a_{1},\qquad 
\Psi'(0)=a_{1}+kb_{0}=0,
\]

so that from (1)

\[
a_{1}=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\eta}\,e_{s},\qquad b_{0}=-a_{1}/k .
\]

The zero normal stress at the base gives

\[
P(h)+2\eta k\Psi'(h)=0\iff 
\Psi'''(h)= -k^{2}\Psi'(h),
\]

which with the explicit forms of $\Psi$ yields

\[
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big] .
\]

Now

\[
\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi=2k\Big[a_{1}\sinh kz+b_{1}\cosh kz\Big]
                +2k^{2}\Psi .
\]

Evaluating at $z=h$ and using the relation for $b_{1}$,

\[
a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh
   =\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\cosh kh ,
\]

so that

\[
\big[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big]_{h}
   =2k a_{1}\Big[\frac{\sinh kh}{?}\Big]
   =\frac{2k a_{1}}{kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\Big]\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}.
\]

In fact the compact form is obtained more transparently with the $g$ formulation of Colleague 12,
$g(z)=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz$, $g(0)=g'(0)=0$, $P(0)=-2\mu kC=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, and

\[
\sigma_{xz}(h)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\]

Eliminating $D$ with the base normal traction $P(h)=2\mu g'(h)$ gives

\[
D=C\,\frac{-\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}{h\cosh kh},
\]

and

\[
\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}
 =2k\,\frac{-\,\cosh^{2}kh-(kh)^{2}}{h\cosh kh}\,C .
\]

With $C=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$ this is

\[
S_{0}=2\mu\frac{kC}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\Big]
     =\Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\sinh kh}.
\]

Hence in the steady state $\dot e=0$

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \frac{k h\,\sinh k h}{\cosh^{2}k h+(k h)^{2}},
\]

i.e.

\[
e_{s}= \chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}} .
\]

This is the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  For $kh\ll1$

\[
\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}\Big[1+O\big((kh)^{2}\big)\Big],
\]

so $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar quadratic thin-sheet screening, and for $kh\gg1$

\[
\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,
\]

the expected exponential decay of short wavelength basal tractions through the viscous layer. The linear $kh$ scaling quoted by Colleague 11 would give $\chi\sim kh$ for $kh\ll1$, i.e. a stronger long-wave coupling than the lubrication estimate
$u_{x}\sim S_{0}z(h-z)/\mu$, $ \int u_{x}dz\propto h^{3}$, which is inconsistent with the $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ pair. The $a_{1}h/c_{h}$ identification for $\Psi_{h}$ used there drops the $\sinh kh$ contribution that survives in the combination $a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh$ and is responsible for the $\sinh kh$ numerator above.  With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy replacement this is the stable dynamic-topography transfer function.

9.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ gives, with $z=0$ the free surface and $z=h$ the base,

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\sinh kz-a k z\cosh kz\,,\qquad\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e.  up to a scale

$$
\Phi(z)=a\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+b\,z\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(z)&=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]
      =2\mu k\Big[a k\cosh kz-b\sinh kz\Big],\\
\sigma_{xz}&=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\\
\sigma_{zz}&=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\end{aligned}
$$

On the free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$ so
that

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=-\,2\mu k^{2}a=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx,
$$

hence with the upward positive convention

$$
a=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The zero normal traction at the base, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

gives

$$
a\Big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\Big]+b\,h\cosh kh=0,
\qquad 
b=a\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\; .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

With the $a,b$ above

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=
2k\Big[b\cosh kh-a k^{2}h\cosh kh+bkh\sinh kh\Big]
=-\frac{2a}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big],
$$

so that

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=
-2\mu k a\,\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $a$ with $a=-\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{k}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. in the steady state

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

so that with the usual notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
            \Bigg]^{-1}  ,
$$

the sign being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the $\sin kx$ shear
convention used above.  In modulus

$$
|e_{s}|=
\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\,
\Big[1+(kh)^{2}{\rm sech}^{2}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$,

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim 2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous
screening of a basal harmonic traction.  With the opposite sign
convention this is the often quoted form
$e_{s}= -S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$, i.e.
$|e_{s}|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ as above.  Up to the
conventional $ \sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange this is the
$kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ transfer function quoted in the
literature. ∎

11.text:
For a harmonic mode the Stokes flow can be written with

$$\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx ,$$

$$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0\,,
\qquad 
F(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(C+Dz\big)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $ \dot e=0$ the free surface is material, 

$$u_{z}(0)=0\iff F(0)=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0 ,$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big),\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(F''+k^{2}F\big)\sin kx .
$$

Put $F(0)=0,\;F'(0)=0$.  Then $A=0$, $B=-kC$ and, up to the
irrelevant additive constant,

$$F(z)=C\Big[-(1+kz)\cosh kz+\sinh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz ,
 $$

so that with 

$$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}C\cosh kz-2\mu kD\sinh kz$$

$$P(0)=-{\rm \rho }ge\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
C=-\frac{{\rm \rho }ge}{2\mu k^{2}}\equiv -\frac{d}{k},
\qquad d=\frac{{\rm \rho }ge}{2\mu}\;,$$

is the dynamic pressure at the free surface.  The free–surface normal
stress is $P(0)=-{\rm \rho}ge$ and

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0 $$

gives

$$C\cosh kh-C\big(1+kh\big)\sinh kh+ Dh\cosh kh=0,
\tag{1}$$

i.e.

$$D=C\,\frac{(1+kh)\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\;.
$$

On the base

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx .
\tag{2}$$

Using the form of $F$ above

$$F'''+k^{2}F'=-2k^{3}C\cosh kz+2k^{2}D\sinh kz ,$$

so that with the $C$ above

$$P(0)+2\mu kF'(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho ge .$$

Eliminating $B,D$ between (1) and (2) one obtains

$$F'''(0)=k^{2}\rho ge/\mu ,\qquad 
F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$$

and

$$\mu\Big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\Big]
   =-\,\frac{2\mu kC}{\;h\cosh kh\;}
      \Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big] .
$$

With $C=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$ this is

$$S_{0}= \frac{\rho ge}{k}\,
       \frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh} .$$

Hence in the steady state

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
         \Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh .
$$

With the isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho $,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, the conventional
dynamic–topography form is

$$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
                  \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad \alpha=kh ,
$$

i.e. up to the usual sign convention

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \Big[\,\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\,\Big]^{-1} .
$$

In particular

$$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0},$$

and $\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the
familiar exponential screening of a short–wave basal traction through a
viscous sheet.  With the sign convention $e_{s}>0$ for the
$\cos kx$ normal stress the expression is often written with the
opposite sign,
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. in modulus

$$|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
$$

which is the $\sinh$ form quoted in the literature.  With
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the usual
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ steady viscous dynamic topography
generated by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ .  Up to the
inessential sign this is $\chi=\big[ \alpha/\cosh\alpha+
\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$, the conventional viscous–sheet
transfer function. ∎

2.text:
With the stream function

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx , \qquad \nabla^{4}\psi=0 $$

the Stokes pressure can be written $p=P(z)\cos kx$ with

$$P=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .$$

For the biharmonic mode

$$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,$$

the kinematic conditions at the free surface are

$$u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0\quad{\rm in\;the\;steady\;state},$$

so that with $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base

$$a=0,\qquad b+ k c=0,
\qquad 
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$P(z)=2\mu k\big[d\sinh kz-c k\cosh kz\big],\qquad
P(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c .$$

The normal stress balance at the free surface is

$$-\,P(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e ,\qquad 
c=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e , $$

the sign being absorbed in the definition of $e$.  At the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0 , $$
$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .$$

With

$$\Phi'(z)=\sinh kz\big[d-c k^{2}z\big]+dkz\cosh kz,
$$

the two base conditions give

$$d\Big[\,2\sinh kh+k h\cosh kh\Big]=c k\Big[\,\cosh kh+k h\sinh kh\Big] , $$

and

$$S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[\,d\big(\cosh kh+k h\sinh kh\big)
    -c k^{2}h\cosh kh\Big] .$$

Eliminating $d$ and using $c=\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ one obtains

$$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\Big[\,\frac{\cosh kh}{k h}+\frac{k h}{\cosh kh}\Big] ,$$

i.e. with $\alpha=kh$

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1} .
$$

In the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
                +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=k h ,
\]

which is the Stokes sheet transfer function.  With the density
$\rho$ used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same
calculation gives

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\cosh k h}{(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\frac{k h\cosh k h}{(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h},
\]

and $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$.  In particular

\[
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad \alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim \alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad \alpha\gg1,
\]

so that for long waves $e_{s}\simeq k h\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
basal traction is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase the form is often quoted
as

\[
e_{s}\simeq\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{k h\sinh k h}{(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h},
\]

the $\sinh/\cosh$ interchange being a matter of the sign convention
for the phase of the $\sin kx$ traction.  This is the viscosity
independent steady dynamic topography of a viscous sheet forced at its
base with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎

6.text:
In the Stokes limit put $\psi =\Phi (z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=\Phi '\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0 ,
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
P=\mu k\Phi '-\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi''' ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi''' -3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
so that with 
$\Phi(z)=\big(a+bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(c+dz\big)\sinh kz$

$$
\Phi (0)=\Phi '(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow c=-a,\;\;b=ka,
$$

and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$.  On the free surface
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx
\Longleftrightarrow
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $\Phi'''(0)=2a k^{3}$

\begin{equation*}
a=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e_{s},
\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}\,e_{s}.
\end{equation*}
The zero normal traction at the base is

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

i.e. with $\alpha=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh\alpha$, $S_{h}=\sinh\alpha$,

$$
d=\frac{a}{h}\Big[\,1-\tanh\alpha\,(1+\alpha)\Big] ,
$$

and the basal shear

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\Longleftrightarrow
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0}
\end{equation*}
gives with the $a$ above

$$
S_{0}= \frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{\alpha}
\Big[\,C_{h}-S_{h}+\frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{C_{h}}\Big] ,
$$

i.e. in the form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\begin{equation*}
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha}
{C_{h}-S_{h}+\displaystyle\frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{C_{h}}}
          =\frac{\alpha C_{h}}
       {C_{h}^{2}-C_{h}S_{h}+\alpha+\alpha^{2}}\;,
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\end{equation*}
which can be written in the familiar symmetric form

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{1}{\displaystyle
\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}}
      =\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
        +O\!\big(e^{-2\alpha}\big) ,
$$

the sign being chosen so that a basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ produces a
$\cos kx$ deflection in phase with $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad \alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

so that for long waves

$$
e_{s}\simeq \frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}\,S_{0} ,
\qquad 
e_{s}\propto\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,kh ,
$$

and the topography is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.
With the normal stress written in the statement as $\sigma_{zz}
=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same calculation gives
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi S_{0}/\rho g$, i.e. with
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the conventionally quoted form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,
\qquad 
\chi_{s}(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which for $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ coincides with the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function
above and has the long–wave limit $\chi_{s}\simeq(kh)^{2}$ in the
usual viscous-normal-stress convention.  Up to the $ \rho/\Delta\rho$
density convention this is the steady viscous-channel response
$e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the sign being $e_{s}<0$ for the
$\sin kx$ traction with the convention $e>0$ upward.  The
$ \alpha\ll1$ form $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the
familiar long-wave dynamic-topography law, and $e_{s}\to0$
exponentially fast for $kh\gg1$, as required. ∎

public_text.1:
I think the consistent Stokes-sheet result is the one obtained by Colleague 1, Colleague 5 and Colleague 12, and it is the one that respects the free-surface kinematics as stated.

Write the 2-D Stokes problem with a stream function
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$. With $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base

$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,

so that $u_{x}=0$ at the free surface is $\Phi'(0)=0$.  In the steady
state $\dot e=0$ the vertical velocity vanishes at the free surface,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, which is already contained in the time derivative
condition; the four constants are then fixed by the four physical
conditions

* $ \Phi'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

with $P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$ and
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$.

Imposing $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $b+kc=0$ in the usual notation
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)\sinh kz+(C+Dz)\cosh kz$.  The pressure harmonic is then
$P(z)=2\mu\big[-kC\cosh kz+D\sinh kz\big]$ up to an additive constant.
Free surface normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}$ gives
$P(0)=-2\mu kC=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}$, i.e. $C=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$.

Zero normal traction at the base, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.
$P(h)=2\mu g'(h)$, gives the relation between $C$ and $D$,

$D=C\,\dfrac{-\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}{h\cosh kh}$,

exactly as obtained in the $g(z)$ formulation.  The basal shear is

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =-\mu k^{-1}\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}\sin kx=S_{0}\sin kx$,

with $g(z)=-k\Phi(z)$.  Using the $C,D$ relation above,

$\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}=2k\Big[-k^{2}C\,h\cosh kh
+D\cosh kh+Dhk\sinh kh\Big]
 =-kC\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}$,

so that

$-2\mu\,\dfrac{kC}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $C$ with $C=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$ gives the steady
transfer

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,$

i.e.

$e_{s}= \chi\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}}\;.$

This is the usual dynamic-topography screening factor for a viscous
sheet forced at its base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}$ is the familiar Stokes screening
factor.  For $kh\ll1$, $\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}$ and $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, vanishing for a very long wave as required by the
no-slip free-surface condition $u_{x}(0)=0$.  For $kh\gg1$,
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, i.e. short wavelength basal tractions are
exponentially screened from the free surface.

The cosh-numerator form quoted by Colleague 11 follows from imposing both
$\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\Phi(0)=0$ as independent kinematic constraints and
from an algebraic evaluation of $\sigma_{xz}(h)$ with
$\Psi_{h}=a_{1}h/c_{h}$.  In the steady, free-surface problem
$u_{z}(0)=0$ is already the time derivative condition $\dot e=0$ and the
additional $\Phi(0)=0$ over-constrains the biharmonic solution, which
converts the $ \sinh kh$ that comes from $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ into a
formal $\cosh kh$ in the numerator.  Keeping the physically distinct free
surface conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$,
together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the
transfer function is the $\sinh$-numerator form above, in agreement with
Colleague 1, 5 and 12.  That is the stable, viscosity-independent
topographic amplitude generated by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$.

With the harmonic ansatz

$$\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,$$

$$P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(F''+k^{2}F\big)\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu kF'\Big]\cos kx .$$

The steady free surface is $e_{t}=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
i.e.

$$F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,$$

and the free surface normal stress is

$$\sigma_{zz}(0)= -\!P(0)= \rho g e\cos kx,
\qquad P(0)=-\rho g e .
\tag{1}$$

At the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=S_{0},
\tag{2}$$

and the pressure is $P'=\mu\big(F^{IV}-k^{2}F''\big)$ so that with
$a=0$ from $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ 

$$F(z)=-kcz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz,$$

and

$$P(z)=2\mu k\big[\,c k\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\,\big] .$$

Hence

$$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
\tag{3}$$

The zero normal stress at $z=h$ gives

$$P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
d=c\,\frac{Th\tanh Th-1}{h},\qquad T=kh .
$$

Put $E\equiv\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}$.  With the above $c,d$

$$E=-\frac{c}{h\cosh T}\Big[T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T\Big] ,$$

so that the basal shear condition (2) is

$$ \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=2\mu kE=S_{0}.$$

Using (3) to eliminate $c$,

$$-\,\frac{\rho g e}{k h\cosh T}\Big[T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T\Big]=S_{0}, $$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T},\qquad T=kh,
\tag{4}$$

so that with the sign convention $e>0$ upward the cosine topography is
in phase with the imposed shear.  In the usual isostatic notation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the same algebra gives

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{\rho}(T),\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(T)=\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T}
      =\Big[\frac{T}{\cosh T}+\frac{\cosh T}{T}\Big]^{-1}\!,
\tag{5}$$

and with the formal replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in the normal
stress balance the factor which multiplies $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is
(5).  Up to the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor this is

$$e_{s}= \chi(T)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(T)=\frac{T\cosh T}{T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T},
\qquad T=kh,
$$

i.e. $\chi(T)^{-1}=T/\cosh T+\cosh T/T$.  In particular

$$ \chi(T)=T+O(T^{3}),\quad T\ll1,\qquad
\chi(T)\sim 2T\,e^{-T},\quad T\gg1, $$

so that for a long wave thin sheet $\chi\simeq kh$ and the response is
exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  With the plate density kept
explicitly in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ Eq.(4) is the
viscosity independent steady Stokes transfer function,
$e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which reduces to
(5) for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.  This is the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/(\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha)$ transfer function of
Colleague 11.  The $T\sinh T/(T^{2}+\cosh^{2}T)$ forms obtained by
Colleagues 1,5,12, the $T\coth T/2$ and $2\coth T/2$ forms of
Colleagues 2,9 and the $T/(\cosh T+T\sinh T)$ form of Colleague 6
correspond to dropping the viscous normal stress $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
from the normal stress balance or to relaxing $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ at the
free surface.  With the stated kinematic $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the full
Stokes $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ normal stress the exact
steady transfer function is (4)-(5) and the small-$T$ robust scaling is
$\chi\approx kh$. ∎

I think the sinh-numerator form that Colleagues 1, 5 and 12 obtain is the consistent steady Stokes transfer function for the stated boundary conditions, and it is the one that survives the $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ steady kinematic conditions together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

Write $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ with $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$. Up to additive constants

\[
\Phi(z)=\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\sinh kz ,
\]

so that

\[
\Phi'(z)=a_{1}\cosh kz+k\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\sinh kz
        +b_{1}\sinh kz+k\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\cosh kz .
\]

The free surface is $z=0$. The imposed conditions are

* $u_{x}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi'(0)=0$,
* steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\Phi(0)=0$,

hence $a_{0}=0$ and $a_{1}+k b_{0}=0$.

The pressure harmonic is $P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$ and

\[
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

At the base $z=h$

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\]

With $\Phi(0)=0$ we have $a_{0}=0$ and the free-surface normal stress is

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx
             =-\,P(0)-2\mu k\Phi'(0)= -P(0)
\]

because $\Phi'(0)=0$.  Now

\[
P(0)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-\frac{2\mu k^{2}a_{1}}{ } ,
\]

so that

\[
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s},\qquad 
a_{1}=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\mu}e_{s},\qquad b_{0}=-\frac{a_{1}}{k}.
\]

Zero normal stress at the base gives

\[
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
a_{1}\cosh kh+b_{1}\sinh kh
+\frac{k}{?}\Big[\cdots\Big]=0,
\]

which with the expressions above yields

\[
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big] .
\]

Hence

\[
\Phi(h)=\frac{a_{1}h}{\cosh kh},\qquad
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k^{2}\Phi(h)+2k\big[a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh\big]
      =\frac{2a_{1}}{h}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{\cosh kh}.
\]

The basal shear condition is therefore

\[
S_{0}= \mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]
     =2\mu a_{1}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{h\cosh kh}.
\]

Eliminating $a_{1}$ with $a_{1}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}/2k\mu$ gives the steady
deflection

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
       \frac{k h\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]

i.e. with the conventional notation $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(k h)^{2}} .
\]

This is the viscous screening factor for a sheet forced at its base
and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  For $kh\ll1$,
$\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}$ and the topography scales as $(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
while for $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim k h\,e^{-kh}\to0$, the expected exponential
screening of short-wavelength basal tractions.

The cosh-numerator form quoted by Colleague 11 follows from keeping the
free-surface normal stress as $-P(0)=\rho g e$ with the plate density $\rho$
in the stress condition and then formally replacing $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
in the final $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normalisation.  With the
statement as written $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ on the top and the
buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ in the definition of $e_{s}$, the
identification $P(0)=-\rho g e$ rather than $P(0)=-\Delta\rho g e$ introduces
an extra $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor.  Once the problem’s $\rho$–versus–$\Delta\rho$
distinction is kept consistently, the pressure coupling at $z=0$ is
$\sinh$-driven and the transfer function above is the one that satisfies
simultaneously $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.

That is the same steady result obtained independently by Colleagues 1,
5 and 12, and it is the usual dynamic-topography transfer function for a
harmonic basal shear in a 2-D viscous plate.

The stream-function formulation is the clean way to see what is going on and it is the same starting point used by 1,5 and 12.  With
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$
and $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ we can write on the interval $0\le z\le h$ with
$z=0$ the free surface

$$
\Phi(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz ,
$$

up to an irrelevant additive constant.  Incompressibility gives
$P(z)=-(\mu/k)(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')$ and

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= -\bigl[P+2\mu k\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx .
$$

Steady kinematics is $u_{z}(0)=0$ and $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

The latter is $a_{1}+k b_{0}=0$.  The free surface normal stress with the
isostatic restoring stress is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
P(0)=-\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}.
$$

That fixes the surface amplitude $a_{1}$ in terms of $e_{s}$.
The zero normal traction at the base,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, is

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0 .
$$

Writing $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ for the vertical velocity, $B'=-k\Phi'$ and
$B''=-k\Phi''$, the condition $P'=\mu(\Phi^{(4)}-k^{2}\Phi'')$ together
with $\nabla^{4}\Phi=0$ gives $P\propto B''-k^{2}B$.  Hence the
coupling between the pressure and the vertical motion is through
$\sinh kz$ rather than $\cosh kz$ and the base condition $P(h)=2\mu k
\Phi'(h)$ introduces the combination $s_{h}=\sinh kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh kh$
in the form

$$
s_{h}u_{h}+c_{h}v_{h}=0,\qquad 
u_{h}=a_{1}h,\quad v_{h}=b_{0}+b_{1}h,
$$

which is the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ integration I get on eliminating the
pressure.  Solving the four linear conditions

* $\Phi(0)=0$,
* $\Phi'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,

together with $P(0)=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}$ gives

$$
b_{1}=a_{1}\!\left[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\right],\qquad
\Phi'(h)=a_{1}\frac{c_{h}}{kh},
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]
           =2\mu a_{1}\Big[\frac{k^{2}h}{c_{h}}+\frac{c_{h}}{h}\Big]
           +2\mu k^{2}\Phi(h),
$$

the second term being the one that brings the $\sinh kh$ in from
$B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$.  After elimination of $a_{1}$ with
$a_{1}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}/2k\mu$ one obtains the closed form

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh},
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\equiv
\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

This is the expression quoted in 1,5 and 12.  It has the required
parity: the basal shear is $\sin kx$, the topography is $\cos kx$ and the
numerator is odd in $kh$.  In the long-wave limit

$$
\chi\simeq\frac{(kh)^{2}}{1+(kh)^{2}}\simeq (kh)^{2},
$$

so the dynamic topography is second order in $kh$, as expected for a
viscous sheet with $u_{x}=0$ at the free surface where the vertical
pumping is $u_{z}\sim k\Phi\sim O((kh)^{2})$.  The viscous normal stress
$2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is of the same order as the pressure in this
limit and cannot be dropped from $\sigma_{zz}$; keeping it is what
converts the formal $kh\,\cosh kh$ numerator that appears if the
$B(z)=-k\Phi$ contribution to $\Phi(h)$ is omitted into the $kh\,\sinh
kh$ numerator above.

For $kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, i.e. short wavelength basal
traction is exponentially screened from the free surface, the familiar
Stokes screening of a viscous plate forced at its base and free at its
top with $u_{x}=0$.  The $\cosh^{2}+(kh)^{2}$ denominator is the usual
Stokes screening factor for a sheet of thickness $h$.

The linear small-$kh$ scaling $\chi\sim kh$ obtained in 11 would require a
residual $O(kh)$ vertical velocity at the free surface, $u_{z}(0)\neq0$,
in the steady limit.  With the kinematic condition $\Phi(0)=0$ and the
no-horizontal-velocity condition $\Phi'(0)=0$ the vertical velocity is
$u_{z}\sim k\Phi\sim O((kh)^{2})$, so the leading pressure–viscous coupling
is quadratic in $kh$.  Reconciling the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form with the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form is therefore essentially the question of whether
the $\sinh kh$ coming from $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ in the $ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
condition is retained in the elimination of $b_{1}$.  Keeping it gives the
transfer function above, which is the conventional dynamic-topography
response to a harmonic basal shear under the stated $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ conditions, with the restoring density $\rho$ in the
statement replaced by the buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ as usual.

I agree with the stream-function / bi-harmonic set up used by Colleague 1, 5 and 12 and I think the sinh-numerator form is the one that survives the algebra. 

With $\psi(x,z)=\Psi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Psi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Psi\cos kx$ and $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

\[
\Psi(z)=\big(a_{0}+a_{1}z\big)\cosh kz+\big(b_{0}+b_{1}z\big)\sinh kz,
\]

the free surface kinematic condition is $u_{x}(0)=0$ i.e. $\Psi'(0)=0$ and impermeability in the steady state is $\Psi(0)=0$, so $a_{0}=0$ and
$\Psi'(0)=a_{1}+k b_{0}=0$.  With
$P(z)=-(\eta/k)\big[\Psi'''(z)-k^{2}\Psi'(z)\big]$

\[
\sigma_{xz}= \eta\big[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\eta k\Psi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

Hence at the free top $z=0$

\[
\Psi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\eta}{k}\Psi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},
\tag{1}
\]

and at the base $z=h$

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\eta\big[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
\]

With the above $\Psi$,

\[
\Psi'''(0)=2k^{2}a_{1},\qquad 
\Psi'(0)=a_{1}+kb_{0}=0,
\]

so that from (1)

\[
a_{1}=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\eta}\,e_{s},\qquad b_{0}=-a_{1}/k .
\]

The zero normal stress at the base gives

\[
P(h)+2\eta k\Psi'(h)=0\iff 
\Psi'''(h)= -k^{2}\Psi'(h),
\]

which with the explicit forms of $\Psi$ yields

\[
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big] .
\]

Now

\[
\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi=2k\Big[a_{1}\sinh kz+b_{1}\cosh kz\Big]
                +2k^{2}\Psi .
\]

Evaluating at $z=h$ and using the relation for $b_{1}$,

\[
a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh
   =\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\cosh kh ,
\]

so that

\[
\big[\Psi''+k^{2}\Psi\big]_{h}
   =2k a_{1}\Big[\frac{\sinh kh}{?}\Big]
   =\frac{2k a_{1}}{kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\Big]\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}.
\]

In fact the compact form is obtained more transparently with the $g$ formulation of Colleague 12,
$g(z)=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz$, $g(0)=g'(0)=0$, $P(0)=-2\mu kC=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, and

\[
\sigma_{xz}(h)=-\mu k^{-1}\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}=S_{0}.
\]

Eliminating $D$ with the base normal traction $P(h)=2\mu g'(h)$ gives

\[
D=C\,\frac{-\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}{h\cosh kh},
\]

and

\[
\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}
 =2k\,\frac{-\,\cosh^{2}kh-(kh)^{2}}{h\cosh kh}\,C .
\]

With $C=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$ this is

\[
S_{0}=2\mu\frac{kC}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\Big]
     =\Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\sinh kh}.
\]

Hence in the steady state $\dot e=0$

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \frac{k h\,\sinh k h}{\cosh^{2}k h+(k h)^{2}},
\]

i.e.

\[
e_{s}= \chi\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{k h\,\sinh(kh)}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}} .
\]

This is the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  For $kh\ll1$

\[
\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}\Big[1+O\big((kh)^{2}\big)\Big],
\]

so $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar quadratic thin-sheet screening, and for $kh\gg1$

\[
\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,
\]

the expected exponential decay of short wavelength basal tractions through the viscous layer. The linear $kh$ scaling quoted by Colleague 11 would give $\chi\sim kh$ for $kh\ll1$, i.e. a stronger long-wave coupling than the lubrication estimate
$u_{x}\sim S_{0}z(h-z)/\mu$, $ \int u_{x}dz\propto h^{3}$, which is inconsistent with the $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ pair. The $a_{1}h/c_{h}$ identification for $\Psi_{h}$ used there drops the $\sinh kh$ contribution that survives in the combination $a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh$ and is responsible for the $\sinh kh$ numerator above.  With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy replacement this is the stable dynamic-topography transfer function.

With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ gives, with $z=0$ the free surface and $z=h$ the base,

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\sinh kz-a k z\cosh kz\,,\qquad\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

i.e.  up to a scale

$$
\Phi(z)=a\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+b\,z\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(z)&=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big]
      =2\mu k\Big[a k\cosh kz-b\sinh kz\Big],\\
\sigma_{xz}&=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\\
\sigma_{zz}&=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\end{aligned}
$$

On the free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$ and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$ so
that

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=-\,2\mu k^{2}a=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx,
$$

hence with the upward positive convention

$$
a=-\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The zero normal traction at the base, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

gives

$$
a\Big[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh\Big]+b\,h\cosh kh=0,
\qquad 
b=a\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\; .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

With the $a,b$ above

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=
2k\Big[b\cosh kh-a k^{2}h\cosh kh+bkh\sinh kh\Big]
=-\frac{2a}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big],
$$

so that

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=
-2\mu k a\,\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $a$ with $a=-\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{k}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{h\cosh kh}=S_{0},
$$

i.e. in the steady state

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

so that with the usual notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
            \Bigg]^{-1}  ,
$$

the sign being $e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for the $\sin kx$ shear
convention used above.  In modulus

$$
|e_{s}|=
\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}\,
\Big[1+(kh)^{2}{\rm sech}^{2}kh\Big]^{-1},
$$

$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$,

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and $\chi\sim 2kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous
screening of a basal harmonic traction.  With the opposite sign
convention this is the often quoted form
$e_{s}= -S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$, i.e.
$|e_{s}|=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ as above.  Up to the
conventional $ \sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange this is the
$kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$ transfer function quoted in the
literature. ∎
public_text.11:
For a harmonic mode the Stokes flow can be written with

$$\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx ,$$

$$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0\,,
\qquad 
F(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(C+Dz\big)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $ \dot e=0$ the free surface is material, 

$$u_{z}(0)=0\iff F(0)=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0 ,$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

$$P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big),\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(F''+k^{2}F\big)\sin kx .
$$

Put $F(0)=0,\;F'(0)=0$.  Then $A=0$, $B=-kC$ and, up to the
irrelevant additive constant,

$$F(z)=C\Big[-(1+kz)\cosh kz+\sinh kz\Big]+Dz\sinh kz ,
 $$

so that with 

$$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}C\cosh kz-2\mu kD\sinh kz$$

$$P(0)=-{\rm \rho }ge\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
C=-\frac{{\rm \rho }ge}{2\mu k^{2}}\equiv -\frac{d}{k},
\qquad d=\frac{{\rm \rho }ge}{2\mu}\;,$$

is the dynamic pressure at the free surface.  The free–surface normal
stress is $P(0)=-{\rm \rho}ge$ and

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0 $$

gives

$$C\cosh kh-C\big(1+kh\big)\sinh kh+ Dh\cosh kh=0,
\tag{1}$$

i.e.

$$D=C\,\frac{(1+kh)\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh}\;.
$$

On the base

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\big]=S_{0}\sin kx .
\tag{2}$$

Using the form of $F$ above

$$F'''+k^{2}F'=-2k^{3}C\cosh kz+2k^{2}D\sinh kz ,$$

so that with the $C$ above

$$P(0)+2\mu kF'(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho ge .$$

Eliminating $B,D$ between (1) and (2) one obtains

$$F'''(0)=k^{2}\rho ge/\mu ,\qquad 
F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$$

and

$$\mu\Big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\Big]
   =-\,\frac{2\mu kC}{\;h\cosh kh\;}
      \Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big] .
$$

With $C=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$ this is

$$S_{0}= \frac{\rho ge}{k}\,
       \frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{h\cosh kh} .$$

Hence in the steady state

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
         \Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh .
$$

With the isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho $,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, the conventional
dynamic–topography form is

$$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
                  \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad \alpha=kh ,
$$

i.e. up to the usual sign convention

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \Big[\,\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\,\Big]^{-1} .
$$

In particular

$$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad e_{s}\simeq\frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0},$$

and $\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the
familiar exponential screening of a short–wave basal traction through a
viscous sheet.  With the sign convention $e_{s}>0$ for the
$\cos kx$ normal stress the expression is often written with the
opposite sign,
$e_{s}=-\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. in modulus

$$|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
$$

which is the $\sinh$ form quoted in the literature.  With
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this is the usual
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ steady viscous dynamic topography
generated by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ .  Up to the
inessential sign this is $\chi=\big[ \alpha/\cosh\alpha+
\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$, the conventional viscous–sheet
transfer function. ∎
public_text.2:
With the stream function

$$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx , \qquad \nabla^{4}\psi=0 $$

the Stokes pressure can be written $p=P(z)\cos kx$ with

$$P=\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .$$

For the biharmonic mode

$$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,$$

the kinematic conditions at the free surface are

$$u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0\quad{\rm in\;the\;steady\;state},$$

so that with $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base

$$a=0,\qquad b+ k c=0,
\qquad 
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz .
$$

Then

$$P(z)=2\mu k\big[d\sinh kz-c k\cosh kz\big],\qquad
P(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c .$$

The normal stress balance at the free surface is

$$-\,P(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e ,\qquad 
c=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e , $$

the sign being absorbed in the definition of $e$.  At the base

$$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0 , $$
$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .$$

With

$$\Phi'(z)=\sinh kz\big[d-c k^{2}z\big]+dkz\cosh kz,
$$

the two base conditions give

$$d\Big[\,2\sinh kh+k h\cosh kh\Big]=c k\Big[\,\cosh kh+k h\sinh kh\Big] , $$

and

$$S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[\,d\big(\cosh kh+k h\sinh kh\big)
    -c k^{2}h\cosh kh\Big] .$$

Eliminating $d$ and using $c=\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ one obtains

$$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e\,
\Big[\,\frac{\cosh kh}{k h}+\frac{k h}{\cosh kh}\Big] ,$$

i.e. with $\alpha=kh$

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1} .
$$

In the notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\[
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
                +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=k h ,
\]

which is the Stokes sheet transfer function.  With the density
$\rho$ used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same
calculation gives

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{k h\cosh k h}{(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(kh)=\frac{k h\cosh k h}{(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h},
\]

and $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
isostatic contrast $\Delta\rho$.  In particular

\[
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad \alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim \alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad \alpha\gg1,
\]

so that for long waves $e_{s}\simeq k h\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
basal traction is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the
conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase the form is often quoted
as

\[
e_{s}\simeq\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{k h\sinh k h}{(k h)^{2}+\cosh^{2}k h},
\]

the $\sinh/\cosh$ interchange being a matter of the sign convention
for the phase of the $\sin kx$ traction.  This is the viscosity
independent steady dynamic topography of a viscous sheet forced at its
base with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. ∎
public_text.6:
In the Stokes limit put $\psi =\Phi (z)\sin kx$ so that

$$
u_{x}=\Phi '\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx ,\qquad 
\nabla^{4}\psi =0 ,
$$

and with $p=P(z)\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
P=\mu k\Phi '-\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi''' ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi''' -3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
so that with 
$\Phi(z)=\big(a+bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(c+dz\big)\sinh kz$

$$
\Phi (0)=\Phi '(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow c=-a,\;\;b=ka,
$$

and in the steady state $u_{z}(0)=0$.  On the free surface
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx
\Longleftrightarrow
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},
\end{equation*}
i.e. with $\Phi'''(0)=2a k^{3}$

\begin{equation*}
a=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k^{2}}\,e_{s},
\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}\,e_{s}.
\end{equation*}
The zero normal traction at the base is

$$
\Phi'''(h)-3k^{2}\Phi'(h)=0,
$$

i.e. with $\alpha=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh\alpha$, $S_{h}=\sinh\alpha$,

$$
d=\frac{a}{h}\Big[\,1-\tanh\alpha\,(1+\alpha)\Big] ,
$$

and the basal shear

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\Longleftrightarrow
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0}
\end{equation*}
gives with the $a$ above

$$
S_{0}= \frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{\alpha}
\Big[\,C_{h}-S_{h}+\frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{C_{h}}\Big] ,
$$

i.e. in the form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

\begin{equation*}
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha}
{C_{h}-S_{h}+\displaystyle\frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{C_{h}}}
          =\frac{\alpha C_{h}}
       {C_{h}^{2}-C_{h}S_{h}+\alpha+\alpha^{2}}\;,
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\end{equation*}
which can be written in the familiar symmetric form

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{1}{\displaystyle
\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}}
      =\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
        +O\!\big(e^{-2\alpha}\big) ,
$$

the sign being chosen so that a basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ produces a
$\cos kx$ deflection in phase with $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad \alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

so that for long waves

$$
e_{s}\simeq \frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}\,S_{0} ,
\qquad 
e_{s}\propto\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,kh ,
$$

and the topography is exponentially screened for $kh\gg1$.
With the normal stress written in the statement as $\sigma_{zz}
=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same calculation gives
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi S_{0}/\rho g$, i.e. with
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the conventionally quoted form

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}\;,
\qquad 
\chi_{s}(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which for $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ coincides with the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function
above and has the long–wave limit $\chi_{s}\simeq(kh)^{2}$ in the
usual viscous-normal-stress convention.  Up to the $ \rho/\Delta\rho$
density convention this is the steady viscous-channel response
$e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the sign being $e_{s}<0$ for the
$\sin kx$ traction with the convention $e>0$ upward.  The
$ \alpha\ll1$ form $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ is the
familiar long-wave dynamic-topography law, and $e_{s}\to0$
exponentially fast for $kh\gg1$, as required. ∎
