\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
      +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},$$

the $180^{\circ}$ phase shift between the $\sin kx$ basal traction and the
$\cos kx$ topography being absorbed in the sign of $e_{s}$.  With the
isostatic restoring stress written as ${\sigma}_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the conventional dynamic–topography transfer function is

$$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}, 
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
      +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh, $$

so that

$$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1, $$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a long wave and exponential
viscous screening for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional sign/phase
convention this is often quoted in modulus form as

$$|e_{s}|=
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{m}(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}, $$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase choice.  With the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
normalisation this is the viscosity independent steady Stokes
transfer function $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a viscous sheet
forced by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
${\sigma}_{zz}(h)=0$ and ${\sigma}_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification. ∎

9.text:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $z=0$ the free
top and $z=h$ the base

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0,\;\Phi(0)=0 ,
$$

i.e. $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and with $\alpha=kh$

$$
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]
     =2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
$$

gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad 
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=-2k^{3}cz\cosh kz
+2kd\big[\cosh kz+kz\sinh kz\big] ,
$$

so that at $z=h$

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=2k\Big[-k^{2}hc\cosh\alpha+d\cosh\alpha
+kdh\sinh\alpha\Big]
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Hence with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] ,
$$

and with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
S_{0}= \frac{\rho g e}{\alpha}\,
      \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\;,
\qquad\alpha=kh .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad 
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent Stokes sheet transfer.  With the
isostatic restoring stress written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos
kx$ the conventional form is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in modulus

$$
\big|e_{s}\big|
 =\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} ,
$$

the sign being $e_{s}\propto -\sin kx$ for the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$
shear.  In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
viscous screening for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional
$\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase choice this is often written in
magnitude form as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual $180^{\circ}$
phase convention between the basal $\sin kx$ shear and the $\cos kx$
topography.  With $\rho=\Delta\rho$ the transfer function is
viscosity independent and reduces to the quoted
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi=[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+
\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$. ∎

public_text.1:
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now essentially agreed on, so the whole issue is the numerator that comes from the evaluation of $\sigma_{xz}(h)$ once the four physical conditions are imposed.

Write $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz ,
$$

$P(z)=-(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state the free surface is material, $u_{z}(0)=0$, and the
imposed kinematic condition is $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so $a_{0}=0$, $a_{1}+k b_{0}=0$.  With $P(0)=-2\mu k^{2}a_{1}$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx
\;\Longrightarrow\;
a_{1}=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\mu}\,e_{s}, \qquad b_{0}=-a_{1}/k .
$$

Zero normal traction at the base,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff 
\Phi'''(h)=-k^{2}\Phi'(h),
$$

gives

$$
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac1{kh}-\tanh kh\Big] .
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[a_{1}\sinh kz+b_{1}\cosh kz\big]+O(z)
$$

and the combination that enters the basal shear is

$$
a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh
   =\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\cosh kh ,
$$

but the shear itself is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =2\mu k\,\frac{a_{1}}{h\cosh kh}
     \Big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\Big]\,
     \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\;,
$$

the explicit $\sinh kh$ coming from the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ part of the
pressure–vertical-velocity coupling, $P\propto B''-k^{2}B$, and from the
$ \sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation $P(h)=2\mu k\Phi'(h)$.  Eliminating $a_{1}$,

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}\; .
$$

Hence in steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\quad
\alpha=kh,
$$

the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its
base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  The phase is $\sin kx\to
\cos kx$, the sign being absorbed in the definition of $e_{s}$.

The long-wave limit is now the lubrication one,

$$
\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
$$

so $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $e_{s}\to0$ for a very
long wave, as required by $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady
state.  For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential screening of short wavelength basal tractions.

The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form quoted by
Colleague 11, 10, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9 follows from evaluating $\sigma_{xz}(h)$
with the identification $\Psi_{h}=a_{1}h/\cosh\alpha$ and dropping the
$a_{1}\sinh\alpha+b_{1}\cosh\alpha$ contribution that survives the
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ coupling.  Imposing both $\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\Phi(0)=0$
as independent conditions and then formally replacing
$P(0)=-\rho g e$ by $P(0)=-\Delta\rho g e$ converts the $\sinh kh$ that
comes from $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ into a formal $\cosh kh$ in the
numerator.  The claim that $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ is the same up to
notation is not correct; the two functions are distinct and the
$\sinh$ numerator is the one that keeps the $B(z)=-k\Phi$ contribution to
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the stated $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same algebra gives
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
and the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement yields the
dynamic-topography transfer function above, in agreement with the
independent derivations of Colleagues 1, 5 and 12. ∎
public_text.12:
With the harmonic ansatz
$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

The stated top conditions are $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the normal stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.  In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the
free surface is material, $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the time–averaged sense, i.e.
$\Phi'(0)=0$ is the independent kinematic condition; $\Phi(0)=0$ is the
integrated-in-time statement $\dot e=0$ and is not an independent
biharmonic constraint.  Imposing the independent conditions

* $\Phi'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

gives, with $a=0$ from $F(0)$ up to an irrelevant additive constant,
$b+kc=0$ from $\Phi'(0)=0$ and

$$
P(0)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=-2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e,
\qquad 
c=\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}}\equiv -\frac{d}{k}.
$$

Writing $g(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ the zero normal traction at the base is
$P(h)=2\mu g'(h)$ and

$$
D=C\,\frac{-\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}{h\cosh kh},
\qquad 
P(0)=-2\mu kC=-\rho g e .
$$

Now

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
  =-\mu k^{-1}\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}
$$

and with the $C,D$ relation above

$$
\big[g''+k^{2}g\big]_{h}
 =2k\,\frac{-\,\cosh^{2}kh-(kh)^{2}}{h\cosh kh}\,C .
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}=2\mu\,\frac{kC}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\Big],
$$

and eliminating $C$ with $C=\rho g e/2\mu k$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh}.
$$

With the isostatic restoring density $\Delta\rho$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, the steady transfer is

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\;
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}
      \equiv\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}(kh)+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

This is the Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its
base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  The numerator is odd in $k$,
as required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$ basal shear
and the $\cos kx$ topography.  In particular

$$
\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}\big[1+O((kh)^{2})\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar quadratic
thin-sheet screening.  With $u_{x}(0)=0$ the vertical pumping is
$u_{z}\sim k\Phi\sim O((kh)^{2})$; a linear $kh$ long-wave limit would
require an $O(kh)$ residual vertical velocity at the free surface,
inconsistent with the steady kinematic condition $\dot e=0$.  For
$kh\gg1$, $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, the expected exponential viscous
screening of short wavelength basal tractions.

The $\,kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form obtained by imposing
both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic
constraints converts the combination $a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh=
a_{1}\cosh kh/kh$ that follows from $b_{1}=a_{1}[1/kh-\tanh kh]$ into a
formal $\cosh$ numerator.  That is the over-constraint
$\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ noted by Colleague 1, and it is
essentially the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ phase convention mentioned by
Colleague 11.  Keeping the physically distinct free-surface conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, together with
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the transfer function is the
$\sinh$-numerator form above, in agreement with Colleagues 1, 5 and 12,
and it reduces to the conventional $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ dynamic
topography with $\chi$ viscosity-independent. ∎
public_text.5:
I think the steady transfer function that satisfies the four physical conditions stated in the problem is the sinh-numerator form that Colleague 1, 5 and 12 obtain, and the cosh-numerator form that appears in Colleague 10/11 is the result of imposing an extra kinematic constraint.

With the harmonic stream function

\[
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
\]

\[
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
\]

The pressure harmonic is $p=P(z)\cos kx$ with

\[
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

For the steady free surface the physical conditions are

* $u_{x}(0)=0\iff \Phi'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

i.e. four conditions for the four constants $a,b,c,d$.  The material
surface condition in the steady limit is $\dot e=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, which
is not an independent condition on $\Phi$ once the pressure is allowed to
adjust; imposing $\Phi(0)=0$ in addition to $\Phi'(0)=0$ is the
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$ pair used by Colleague 10/11 and it over-constrains the
biharmonic solution.  With only $\Phi'(0)=0$ one may write
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)\sinh kz+(C+Dz)\cosh kz$ with $A=0$, $B+kC=0$ and

\[
P(z)=2\mu k^{2}C\cosh kz-2\mu kD\sinh kz,
\qquad P(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}.
\]

The zero normal traction at the base,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, gives

\[
C\cosh kh-C(1+kh)\sinh kh+Dh\cosh kh=0,
\qquad 
D=C\frac{(1+kh)\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh},
\]

exactly the $g(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ relation used in the $g$ formulation.
The basal shear is

\[
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0},
\]

and with the $C,D$ relation above

\[
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kC}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big]
   \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}.
\]

Eliminating $C=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$ gives the steady transfer

\[
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh},
\]

i.e.

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(kh),\qquad 
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
\]

This is the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at
its base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  The denominator
$\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}$ is the familiar screening denominator and the
numerator is $\sinh kh$, coming from $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ in the
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ condition.  Dropping the $\sinh$ contribution that
comes from $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$ is precisely what turns the
numerator into $\cosh kh$ in the over-constrained $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ calculation.

Asymptotically

\[
\chi\simeq (kh)^{2}\big[1+O((kh)^{2})\big],\qquad kh\ll1,
\]
\[
\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\qquad kh\gg1,
\]

so $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for long waves and the
topography is exponentially screened for short waves.  The linear
$kh$ long-wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$ quoted for the cosh-numerator form
would require a residual $O(kh)$ vertical velocity at the free surface,
$u_{z}(0)\neq0$, in the steady limit, which is inconsistent with
$\dot e=0$ and with the lubrication expectation
$u_{x}\sim S_{0}z(h-z)/\mu$, $\int u_{x}dz\propto h^{3}$.

The statement writes the free-surface normal stress as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and the final amplitude is requested
with the buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity in the conventional isostatic
identification and does not change the $kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$
structure; the apparent $\cosh$ numerator in Colleague 10/11 is the same
algebra with the extra independent condition $\Phi(0)=0$ imposed and with
the $\rho$ versus $\Delta\rho$ normalisation moved to the end.  Keeping
the four physical conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the stable steady
dynamic-topography amplitude is the sinh-numerator form above, in agreement
with Colleague 1, 5 and 12.
public_text.7:
The algebra we now have for the biharmonic stream function is essentially unanimous and that is good progress.  With

$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$,

the four physical conditions for the steady mode are
$u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$.  In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the
impermeability condition is $e_t=0$, i.e. $u_z(0)=0$ as a consequence of
the steady topography, not as an independent kinematic constraint on
$F$.  The independent kinematic condition at the free surface is
$u_x(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$, and $F(0)$ is then set by the pressure jump
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$.

Imposing the extra independent condition $F(0)=0$, i.e. $u_z(0)=0$ as a
second independent condition, gives $A=0$, $B=-kC$ and
$F(z)=C[-(1+kz)\cosh kz+\sinh kz]+Dz\sinh kz$.
With that over-constrained set one obtains the compact form

$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho g e$, 
$D=C[(1+kh)\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/h\cosh kh$,

and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=-\frac{2\mu kC}{h\cosh kh}\big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\big]
=S_0$,

i.e. formally

$e_{s}= \frac{S_0}{\rho g}\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$.

That is the expression quoted by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,8,9.  The
formal $kh\cosh kh$ numerator is the result of using $F(0)=0$ and
$F'(0)=0$ as two independent conditions.  If the steady kinematic
condition is kept as the usual $e_t=0$ and the only independent
free-surface kinematic condition is $u_x(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$, the
integration constant $F(0)$ is not set to zero independently.  The
pressure harmonic is then $P(0)=-2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho g e$ with
$C=\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and the base normal traction $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
gives $b_{1}=a_{1}[1/kh-\tanh kh]$ for the conventional notation
$\Phi(z)=(a_0+a_1z)\cosh kz+(b_0+b_1z)\sinh kz$, $a_0=0$, $a_1+kb_0=0$.

Evaluating

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$,

one finds

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2k a_{1}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{h\cosh kh}
\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}$,

and with $a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2k\mu$ the base shear condition gives

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\sinh kh}$,

i.e. in the conventional $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}.$

This is the transfer function obtained by Colleagues 1,5,12 and 7.
It satisfies $u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ with the steady condition $e_t=0$, and it has the
required physical limits: $\chi\simeq(kh)^{2}$ for $kh\ll1$, so the
topography vanishes quadratically for a very long wave as required by
$u_x(0)=0$, and $\chi\sim kh e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar
exponential screening of short wavelength basal tractions.

The $kh\cosh kh$ form is algebraically identical to the above up to the
conventional $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ phase/sign absorbed in the
definition of $e$, and it is the same result with the identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ in the normal stress balance
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ versus the isostatic definition
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Keeping the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$
distinction explicit the formal result with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$
is $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$, i.e.
$\chi_{\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$.
With the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ this
reduces to the modulus quoted above, and the $\sinh$ numerator is the
physical, viscosity independent steady dynamic topography for the stated
$u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ problem. ∎
public_text.2:
With the harmonic mode

$ \psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx$,  $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,  $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$,

\begin{equation*}
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz , 
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx, 
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx .
\end{equation*}
The steady free surface is material,

$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ with $z=0$ at the free
surface and $z=h$ at the base.  Hence

$a=0,\qquad b+kc=0$,
\begin{equation*}
F(z)=b\Big[z\cosh kz-\frac{\sinh kz}{k}\Big]+dz\sinh kz , 
\end{equation*}
and

\begin{equation*}
P(z)=-2\mu k\big[\,b\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\,\big] .
\end{equation*}
The normal stress at the free surface is

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g\,e\cos kx$,

\begin{equation*}
-P(0)=2\mu k b=\rho g\,e , \qquad 
b=\frac{\rho g\,e}{2\mu k}\;,
\end{equation*}
the sign being absorbed in the definition of $e$.  The zero normal
traction at the base,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, gives

\begin{equation*}
-b\cosh kh+k b h\sinh kh+d k h\cosh kh=0,
\end{equation*}
i.e.

\begin{equation*}
d=b\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}\;.
\end{equation*}
Now

\begin{equation*}
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[kb z\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dk z\sinh kz\Big],
\end{equation*}
so that with $a=kh$, $C_{a}=\cosh a$,

\begin{equation*}
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =2k\Big[kb hC_{a}+dC_{a}+dkhS_{a}\Big]
 =\frac{2kb}{khC_{a}}\Big[C_{a}^{2}+a^{2}\Big],
\end{equation*}
and

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}\sin kx
 = \frac{2\mu b}{hC_{a}}\big[C_{a}^{2}+a^{2}\big]\sin kx .
\end{equation*}
With $b=\rho ge/2\mu k$ the imposed basal shear
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ gives

\begin{equation*}
S_{0}= \frac{\rho g e}{k h C_{a}}\big[C_{a}^{2}+a^{2}\big] ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

\begin{equation*}
 e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;,
\qquad a=kh ,
\end{equation*}
viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ the conventional dynamic
topography transfer function is

\begin{equation*}
e_{s}= \chi(a)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a}
       =\Bigg[\frac{a}{\cosh a}+\frac{\cosh a}{a}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad a=kh,
\end{equation*}
up to the inessential $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor,
$e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
$\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$.  In modulus

\[
\chi_{\rho}(a)=\frac{a\cosh a}{a^{2}+\cosh^{2}a},\qquad 
 \chi_{\rho}^{-1}=a/\cosh a+\cosh a/a,
\]

and

\[
\chi(a)=a+O(a^{3}),\qquad a\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(a)\sim a e^{-a}\to0,\qquad a\gg1,
\]

so that for long waves $kh\ll1$

\[
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\]

and the short wavelength basal traction is exponentially screened,
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$, through the viscous sheet.  With the usual
sign convention the magnitude is often quoted as

\[
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]

the $\sinh\!\leftrightarrow\!\cosh$ interchange being the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase convention.  The viscosity drops
out of the steady amplitude, which is the familiar $[\,a/\cosh a+
\cosh a/a\,]^{-1}$ Stokes sheet screening factor.  For
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
steady dynamic topography generated by the harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$. ∎
public_text.10:
In the harmonic mode put with $z=0$ at the top and $z=h$ at the base

$$
\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx,
\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

so that $\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ and

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[F'''-k^{2}F'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the free surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0,\qquad 
\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kF(0)=0\;\;\hbox{in the steady state}\iff F(0)=0,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
P(0)=-\rho ge .
$$

With $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

$F(0)=F'(0)=0$ gives $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$$
F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big] ,
$$

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The zero normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0
$$

gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$
$$
d=-c\,\frac{\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
$$

Now

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[-c k^{2}z\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+d kz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that at $z=h$

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=2k\Big[d\cosh\alpha
-c k^{2}h\cosh\alpha+d\alpha\sinh\alpha\Big]
=-\frac{2k c}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big].
$$

Hence

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
   =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
     \Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big]=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

With $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \frac{\rho g e}{k}\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{h\cosh\alpha}
     =\rho g e\,\frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
                     {\alpha\cosh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the $180^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$ basal shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography being absorbed in the sign.  In modulus

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
           +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}\!.
$$

With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional
dynamic-topography transfer function is

$$
 e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

and for the usual identification $\rho\simeq\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
                 +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

so that with the sign absorbed

$$
e_{s}\approx \frac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

and

$$
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad kh\gg1 ,
$$

the familiar viscous screening of a harmonic basal traction through a
sheet of thickness $h$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.  Up to the conventional
$\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign this is often quoted in magnitude as
$\chi_{m}= \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, the
$\sinh\!\leftrightarrow\!\cosh$ interchange being the usual $180^{\circ}$
phase convention for the $S_{0}\sin kx$ traction.  The transfer function
is viscosity independent. ∎
public_text.6:
In the harmonic mode

$$ \psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx , $$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives

$$\Phi(z)=\big(a+bz\big)\cosh kz+\big(c+dz\big)\sinh kz , $$

$$p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big], $$

$${\sigma}_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,
\qquad 
{\sigma}_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx . $$
With $z=0$ the free surface and $z=h$ the base the steady material
surface is

$$u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,$$

so that with $a=0$

$$\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz , $$

$$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz , $$

$$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge .$$

Hence

$$c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'(0)=0 ,$$

and on the base

$${\sigma}_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$$

gives

$$d=c\,\frac{kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh}{h\cosh kh} .$$

Now

$$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi
   =2k\Big[d\cosh kz-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

so that with the $d$ above

$$\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
   =-\frac{2c}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big] .$$

Hence

$$S_{0}
 =\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2\mu k c}{h\cosh kh}\Big[\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}\Big], $$

and with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$

$$S_{0}= \rho g e\;
       \frac{\cosh^{2}kh+k^{2}h^{2}}{kh\cosh kh}. $$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ therefore

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad
\alpha\equiv kh,$$

i.e. in modulus

$$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
      +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},$$

the $180^{\circ}$ phase shift between the $\sin kx$ basal traction and the
$\cos kx$ topography being absorbed in the sign of $e_{s}$.  With the
isostatic restoring stress written as ${\sigma}_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the conventional dynamic–topography transfer function is

$$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}, 
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
      +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh, $$

so that

$$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1, $$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a long wave and exponential
viscous screening for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional sign/phase
convention this is often quoted in modulus form as

$$|e_{s}|=
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{m}(kh)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}, $$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase choice.  With the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
normalisation this is the viscosity independent steady Stokes
transfer function $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a viscous sheet
forced by the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
${\sigma}_{zz}(h)=0$ and ${\sigma}_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification. ∎
public_text.9:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with $z=0$ the free
top and $z=h$ the base

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0,\;\Phi(0)=0 ,
$$

i.e. $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and with $\alpha=kh$

$$
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]
     =2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

On the top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=\rho g e\cos kx ,
\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
$$

gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad 
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=-2k^{3}cz\cosh kz
+2kd\big[\cosh kz+kz\sinh kz\big] ,
$$

so that at $z=h$

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=2k\Big[-k^{2}hc\cosh\alpha+d\cosh\alpha
+kdh\sinh\alpha\Big]
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Hence with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] ,
$$

and with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
S_{0}= \frac{\rho g e}{\alpha}\,
      \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\;,
\qquad\alpha=kh .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\;
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad 
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent Stokes sheet transfer.  With the
isostatic restoring stress written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos
kx$ the conventional form is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in modulus

$$
\big|e_{s}\big|
 =\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} ,
$$

the sign being $e_{s}\propto -\sin kx$ for the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$
shear.  In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
viscous screening for $kh\gg1$.  Up to the conventional
$\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase choice this is often written in
magnitude form as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} ,
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual $180^{\circ}$
phase convention between the basal $\sin kx$ shear and the $\cos kx$
topography.  With $\rho=\Delta\rho$ the transfer function is
viscosity independent and reduces to the quoted
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi=[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+
\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes sheet is $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, 
$P=-(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
Free surface $z=0$ : $u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
base $z=h$ : $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the material surface is $u_z(0)=0$,
i.e. $F(0)=0$.  With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ 
$a=0,\;b=-kc$ and
$F=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$.
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$ gives $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$d=c\,[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/[h\cosh kh]$.
Then
$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -2k c\,[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]/[h\cosh kh]$
and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}
 =-\,2\mu k c\,[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.
Eliminating $c$,
$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$,
$\alpha=kh$,
i.e. up to the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign
$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$,
viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with in modulus
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
and the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ form
$\chi(\alpha)=\rho/\Delta\rho\;\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
For $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
$\chi^{-1}= \alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha$,
$\chi=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$,
so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential Stokes
screening for $kh\gg1$.
The $180^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography is usually absorbed in the sign, so the magnitude is
often quoted as
$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/(\Delta\rho g)\;\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
i.e. $\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
which is the same transfer function up to the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$
phase convention.
Colleague 1,5,12 now insist on the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
numerator and a $ \chi\simeq\alpha^{2}$ long-wave limit, obtained by
keeping $u_{x}(0)=0$ as the only independent free-surface kinematic
condition and treating the viscous normal stress $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
in $\sigma_{zz}$ differently.  That is the $\sinh$-numerator / quadratic
long-wave variant and is algebraically equivalent to the $\cosh$-numerator
form up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign/phase and the
choice of whether $F(0)=0$ is imposed as an independent biharmonic
constraint.  The $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ over-constrained set used by Colleagues
10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 gives the compact $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression above with the linear $kh$ long-wave limit,
which is the viscosity-independent steady dynamic-topography transfer
function normally quoted for a viscous sheet with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.
The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation remains the only inessential density
factor. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function with $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$ gives
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$P= -\mu k^{-1}\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big)$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx$.
In the steady material limit $e_{t}=0$,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ i.e. $F'(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and
$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$.
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$, $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c\big[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha\big]/h\cosh\alpha$,
$\alpha=kh$.

Then
$F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\big]$,
$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}= -2kc\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$,
so
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -2\mu kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha=S_{0}$.
With $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,$

viscosity independent, $180^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.
In modulus

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi_{\rho}^{-1}=\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha$,

$\chi_{\rho}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rho}\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.
Writing the free-surface restoring stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
Up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign/phase this is often quoted in
magnitude as $\chi_{m}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, the
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the $180^{\circ}$ phase between the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography. The $\cosh^{2}+\alpha^{2}$
denominator is now unanimous in the discussion.

The long-wave limit with the full Stokes $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is
linear, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, not $(kh)^{2}$. The $\alpha^{2}$ long-wave
scaling $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}$ and the sinh-numerator form
$\chi_{s}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ arise from keeping
$\Phi'(0)=0$ but treating $\Phi(0)=0$ as an independent biharmonic constraint,
i.e. from dropping the $B(z)=-kF$ contribution to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.
Imposing the four physical conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ with the steady kinematic $e_{t}=0$
gives the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function
above; the sinh-numerator expression is the same transfer function up to sign
and the usual $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase convention.

The $\rho$ versus $\Delta\rho$ normalisation remains a notational point: with
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ the bare transfer is $S_{0}/\rho g$, and the
conventionally quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor
$\Delta\rho/\rho$, unity for the usual isostatic identification.
Viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude. ∎

\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},\qquad
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\;\;\alpha=kh.$$

Viscosity cancels.  Writing the restoring stress as 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$ \chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh, $$

and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},\qquad
\chi\sim\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\alpha\gg1.$$

The $180^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is absorbed in the sign.
In modulus the transfer function is conventionally quoted as

$$|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual sign/phase
convention.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity for the isostatic
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ convention.

Disagreement in round 2: Colleagues 1,5,12 keep only $\Phi'(0)=0$ as an
independent kinematic condition and treat $\Phi(0)=0$ as the integrated
$\dot e=0$ statement, obtaining

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\chi\simeq\alpha^{2},\;\alpha\ll1,$$

the $\sinh$-numerator form. This is the same algebra with the extra
independent condition $\Phi(0)=0$ removed and is the magnitude form
quoted above up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase.  The
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression is the
one that follows from imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e.
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady material surface, and is the
viscosity-independent Stokes screening factor used in the present
derivation.  The long-wave linear scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
and exponential screening $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$ are retained
in either convention. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes stream function can be written
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, 
$P= -(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.

The four physical boundary conditions are
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In the time dependent problem $ \dot e =u_{z}(0)=-kF(0)$,
so that in the steady limit $\dot e=0$ the material surface condition is
$F(0)=0$ and the four constants together with $e_{s}$ are closed.
With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ one may set $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$,

so that $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$\alpha=kh$, i.e. $d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]$

and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $c$ gives the viscosity independent steady transfer

$S_{0}= \rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. up to the usual $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
and for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$.

Hence $\chi=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar viscous
Stokes screening.  The magnitude is often quoted with the $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase absorbed,

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
i.e. the $\sinh$ numerator form of Colleagues 1,5,12.  The two forms differ
only by the conventional $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign and by whether the
steady kinematic condition $F(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, is imposed as an
independent biharmonic condition or as the steady limit $\dot e=0$ of
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)$.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ independently gives the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer above, which is
the solution quoted by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,8,9.  Dropping the independent
$F(0)=0$ constraint and keeping only the four physical conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form quoted by Colleagues 1,5,12, with the long wave
limit $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}$, $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now essentially agreed on;
the remaining disagreement is the numerator $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ and the
associated long wave scaling $\chi\sim\alpha$ vs $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$,
which is the phase/sign convention associated with the independent
imposition of $u_{z}(0)=0$.  The viscosity drops out of the steady
amplitude and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the usual change from the
plate density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ to the isostatic
buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$. ∎

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function can be written with $z=0$ at the free top
and $z=h$ at the base as $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the four
constants $(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$

\[
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

In the steady material surface $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$ so that with the
kinematic top condition $u_{x}(0)=0$

\[
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
\]

i.e. $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and

\[
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz .
\]

Then

\[
P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz,\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c .
\]

Free surface normal stress

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx
\]

gives

\[
c=-\frac{\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
\]

Zero normal traction at the base

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\]

gives with $\alpha=kh$

\[
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
\]

Now

\[
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-k^{2}c\,z\cosh kz
+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
\]

and at $z=h$

\[
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big] .
\]

Hence with the imposed basal shear

\[
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\]

\[
S_{0}= -\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]
      =\frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big] .
\]

In the time independent limit $e=e_{s}$,

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

i.e. with the sign absorbed in the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow
\cos kx$ phase

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\]

viscosity independent.  Writing the restoring stress at the free
surface as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional
isostatic form is

\[
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\]

and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
\]

so that $\chi\simeq kh+O((kh)^{3})$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $180^{\circ}$ phase
between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography
is normally absorbed in the sign and quoted in magnitude as

\[
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{m}=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase convention.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
factor is unity for the conventional isostatic replacement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is
now unanimous; the remaining debate in round 2 is the numerator
$\cosh\alpha$ versus $\sinh\alpha$, i.e. the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ over-
constraint versus the independent $u_{x}(0)=0$ kinematic condition.
With the physically independent steady conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the transfer function above is the viscosity
independent steady Stokes sheet response, in agreement with the
derivation of Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 3, 6, 8, 9 and with the $\sinh$
numerator form of Colleagues 1,5,12 up to the conventional phase/sign. ∎

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic sheet can be written with $\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, 
$P(z)=-(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$.
With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base the steady material free surface gives the
independent kinematic condition $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ and in the
steady limit $\dot e=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$.  With $a=0$, $b=-kc$

$\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu k d\sinh kz$,

$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$, $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$,
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+h d\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$.

Then

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2k c[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[h\cosh\alpha]$

and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$,

$S_{0}= \rho ge\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$,

in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$, viscosity independent.  Writing the restoring stress as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives the conventional
density-normalised form

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
           =[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,
$\chi\simeq\alpha$, $\alpha\ll1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$,
$\alpha\gg1$.

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is conventionally
absorbed in the sign of $e_{s}$.  In modulus the expression is often
quoted as

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual phase
convention.  The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
form is the one obtained if the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ contribution to
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is kept in the evaluation of $[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}$,
i.e. with the independent conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho
ge$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and the steady
$\dot e=0$ condition only.  Imposing the extra independent biharmonic
constraint $\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ converts the formal
$\sinh$ numerator into the $\cosh$ numerator above; the two forms are
identical up to sign/phase and the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$
density normalisation.  The long-wave lubrication limit is
$\chi\sim\alpha$ for the $\cosh$ convention and $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ for
the magnitude $\sinh$ convention, and in all cases $\chi\to0$
exponentially for $kh\gg1$, the familiar viscous screening of a basal
harmonic traction.  The viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic sheet can be written with 
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, 
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$F=(A+Bz)\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
On the free top $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $F'(0)=0$, $B+kC=0$, and 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ is $-P(0)=\rho g e$ on the steady
material surface.  In the steady state $\dot e=0$ implies 
$u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$, $A=0$, $F(z)=Bz\cosh kz+(C+Dz)\sinh kz$,
$B=-kC$.

With the four physical conditions $F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ one gets
$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}C\cosh kz-2\mu kD\sinh kz$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho ge$,
$D=C[ kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/[h\cosh kh]$ and

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -2kC[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]/[h\cosh kh]$,

so that with $C=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$

$S_{0}= \rho ge\,[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$, 
$\alpha=kh$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ material steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
and for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}
=[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

$\chi\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx$–$\cos kx$ phase is normally absorbed in the
sign.  In modulus this is the oft quoted

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}$,

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the conventional phase
convention.

The split in the round is the $F(0)=0$ vs $F'(0)=0$ only issue.
Colleagues 1,5,12 keep the independent free-surface kinematic condition
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and the steady impermeability $u_{z}(0)=0$ as $F(0)=0$,
$F'(0)=0$ and obtain the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
magnitude with a $kh^{2}$ long-wave limit $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}
/\Delta\rho g$.  Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,7,8,9 impose the material
condition $F(0)=0$ together with $F'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic
constraints and obtain the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
form with the linear long-wave limit $e_{s}\simeq khS_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The two forms are the same transfer function up to the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign and the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation.  The denominator
$\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now essentially agreed on; the remaining
disagreement is the $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ numerator and the
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ factor.  The viscosity drops out of the steady
amplitude. ∎

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady Stokes mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$\big(D^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}F=0$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-(\mu/k)\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big)$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(F''+k^{2}F\big)\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx$ .

On the free top $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and in the
steady state $\dot e=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$. With $z=0$ top,
$z=h$ base

$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $a=0$, $b=-kc$,

$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,

$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$,
$c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, i.e.

$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+h d\cosh\alpha=0$,
$\alpha=kh$,

$d=-c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=2k\big[d\cosh\alpha+d\alpha\sinh\alpha
-k^{2}ch\cosh\alpha\big]
=-\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$.

Hence with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$

$S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\dfrac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]
     =\rho ge\,\dfrac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
       +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},\qquad\alpha=kh,$

the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in
the sign, $e_{s}=-\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ in the sign convention used
above.  The viscosity drops out.  With the isostatic restoring stress
written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$.

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}
/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the
usual viscous screening.

The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form quoted by
Colleagues 1,5,12 is the same transfer function up to the conventional
$\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase/sign. With the magnitude convention
$e_{s}>0$ for the $\cos kx$ normal stress the magnitude is often written

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
         \dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$
for $\alpha\gg1$.  The $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange is the
$180^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the
$\cos kx$ dynamic topography and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the
conventional change from the plate density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$ to the isostatic buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$.  The
over-constrained $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ calculation gives the compact
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression above; dropping
the $F(0)=0$ independent condition converts the numerator to the
commonly quoted $\sinh$ form. ∎

reflection_text.2:
The harmonic Stokes sheet is $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, 
$P=-(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
Free surface $z=0$ : $u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
base $z=h$ : $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the material surface is $u_z(0)=0$,
i.e. $F(0)=0$.  With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ 
$a=0,\;b=-kc$ and
$F=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$.
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$ gives $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$d=c\,[kh\sinh kh-\cosh kh]/[h\cosh kh]$.
Then
$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -2k c\,[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]/[h\cosh kh]$
and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}
 =-\,2\mu k c\,[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$.
Eliminating $c$,
$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$,
$\alpha=kh$,
i.e. up to the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign
$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$,
viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with in modulus
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
and the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ form
$\chi(\alpha)=\rho/\Delta\rho\;\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
For $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
$\chi^{-1}= \alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha$,
$\chi=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$,
so $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential Stokes
screening for $kh\gg1$.
The $180^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography is usually absorbed in the sign, so the magnitude is
often quoted as
$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/(\Delta\rho g)\;\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
i.e. $\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
which is the same transfer function up to the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$
phase convention.
Colleague 1,5,12 now insist on the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
numerator and a $ \chi\simeq\alpha^{2}$ long-wave limit, obtained by
keeping $u_{x}(0)=0$ as the only independent free-surface kinematic
condition and treating the viscous normal stress $2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$
in $\sigma_{zz}$ differently.  That is the $\sinh$-numerator / quadratic
long-wave variant and is algebraically equivalent to the $\cosh$-numerator
form up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign/phase and the
choice of whether $F(0)=0$ is imposed as an independent biharmonic
constraint.  The $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ over-constrained set used by Colleagues
10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 gives the compact $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression above with the linear $kh$ long-wave limit,
which is the viscosity-independent steady dynamic-topography transfer
function normally quoted for a viscous sheet with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.
The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation remains the only inessential density
factor. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The biharmonic stream function with $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$ gives
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$P= -\mu k^{-1}\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big)$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx$.
In the steady material limit $e_{t}=0$,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$ i.e. $F'(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and
$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$.
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$, $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c\big[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha\big]/h\cosh\alpha$,
$\alpha=kh$.

Then
$F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\big]$,
$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}= -2kc\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$,
so
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -2\mu kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha=S_{0}$.
With $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,$

viscosity independent, $180^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$.
In modulus

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi_{\rho}^{-1}=\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha$,

$\chi_{\rho}=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rho}\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.
Writing the free-surface restoring stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
Up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign/phase this is often quoted in
magnitude as $\chi_{m}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, the
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the $180^{\circ}$ phase between the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography. The $\cosh^{2}+\alpha^{2}$
denominator is now unanimous in the discussion.

The long-wave limit with the full Stokes $\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu\partial_{z}u_{z}$ is
linear, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, not $(kh)^{2}$. The $\alpha^{2}$ long-wave
scaling $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}$ and the sinh-numerator form
$\chi_{s}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ arise from keeping
$\Phi'(0)=0$ but treating $\Phi(0)=0$ as an independent biharmonic constraint,
i.e. from dropping the $B(z)=-kF$ contribution to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.
Imposing the four physical conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ with the steady kinematic $e_{t}=0$
gives the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function
above; the sinh-numerator expression is the same transfer function up to sign
and the usual $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase convention.

The $\rho$ versus $\Delta\rho$ normalisation remains a notational point: with
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ the bare transfer is $S_{0}/\rho g$, and the
conventionally quoted $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor
$\Delta\rho/\rho$, unity for the usual isostatic identification.
Viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude. ∎

reflection_text.6:
The Stokes sheet is written with 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.  With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base

$$\Phi=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],$$

$$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
$$

Free surface: $u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the material surface gives $u_{z}(0)=0$
$\iff\Phi(0)=0$.  Then $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$$\Phi(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz, $$

$$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big],
\qquad P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e .$$

Hence $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$c\cosh\alpha-c\alpha\sinh\alpha+d h\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$
$$d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
$$

With
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[d\cosh kz-k^{2}cz\cosh kz
+dkz\sinh kz\big]$

$$\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big] .
$$

Therefore

$$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]=S_{0} ,$$

and with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$

$$S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},\qquad
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\;\;\alpha=kh.$$

Viscosity cancels.  Writing the restoring stress as 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$ \chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh, $$

and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},\qquad
\chi\sim\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\alpha\gg1.$$

The $180^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ is absorbed in the sign.
In modulus the transfer function is conventionally quoted as

$$|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual sign/phase
convention.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity for the isostatic
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ convention.

Disagreement in round 2: Colleagues 1,5,12 keep only $\Phi'(0)=0$ as an
independent kinematic condition and treat $\Phi(0)=0$ as the integrated
$\dot e=0$ statement, obtaining

$$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\chi\simeq\alpha^{2},\;\alpha\ll1,$$

the $\sinh$-numerator form. This is the same algebra with the extra
independent condition $\Phi(0)=0$ removed and is the magnitude form
quoted above up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase.  The
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression is the
one that follows from imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e.
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady material surface, and is the
viscosity-independent Stokes screening factor used in the present
derivation.  The long-wave linear scaling $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
and exponential screening $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$ are retained
in either convention. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The harmonic Stokes stream function can be written
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, 
$P= -(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.

The four physical boundary conditions are
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In the time dependent problem $ \dot e =u_{z}(0)=-kF(0)$,
so that in the steady limit $\dot e=0$ the material surface condition is
$F(0)=0$ and the four constants together with $e_{s}$ are closed.
With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ one may set $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$,

so that $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$\alpha=kh$, i.e. $d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]$

and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$.

Eliminating $c$ gives the viscosity independent steady transfer

$S_{0}= \rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. up to the usual $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$.

With the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
and for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$.

Hence $\chi=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar viscous
Stokes screening.  The magnitude is often quoted with the $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase absorbed,

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
i.e. the $\sinh$ numerator form of Colleagues 1,5,12.  The two forms differ
only by the conventional $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign and by whether the
steady kinematic condition $F(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, is imposed as an
independent biharmonic condition or as the steady limit $\dot e=0$ of
$\dot e=u_{z}(0)$.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ independently gives the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer above, which is
the solution quoted by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,8,9.  Dropping the independent
$F(0)=0$ constraint and keeping only the four physical conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form quoted by Colleagues 1,5,12, with the long wave
limit $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}$, $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now essentially agreed on;
the remaining disagreement is the numerator $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ and the
associated long wave scaling $\chi\sim\alpha$ vs $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$,
which is the phase/sign convention associated with the independent
imposition of $u_{z}(0)=0$.  The viscosity drops out of the steady
amplitude and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the usual change from the
plate density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ to the isostatic
buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$. ∎
reflection_text.9:
The biharmonic stream function can be written with $z=0$ at the free top
and $z=h$ at the base as $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.  With the four
constants $(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$

\[
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx .
\]

In the steady material surface $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$ so that with the
kinematic top condition $u_{x}(0)=0$

\[
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad\Phi'(0)=0,
\]

i.e. $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and

\[
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz .
\]

Then

\[
P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz,\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c .
\]

Free surface normal stress

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx
\]

gives

\[
c=-\frac{\rho g\,e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e .
\]

Zero normal traction at the base

\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\]

gives with $\alpha=kh$

\[
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
\]

Now

\[
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-k^{2}c\,z\cosh kz
+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
\]

and at $z=h$

\[
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big] .
\]

Hence with the imposed basal shear

\[
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
\]

\[
S_{0}= -\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]
      =\frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big] .
\]

In the time independent limit $e=e_{s}$,

\[
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

i.e. with the sign absorbed in the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow
\cos kx$ phase

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\]

viscosity independent.  Writing the restoring stress at the free
surface as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional
isostatic form is

\[
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\]

and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

\[
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
\]

so that $\chi\simeq kh+O((kh)^{3})$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  The $180^{\circ}$ phase
between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography
is normally absorbed in the sign and quoted in magnitude as

\[
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},\qquad
\chi_{m}=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
\]

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase convention.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
factor is unity for the conventional isostatic replacement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is
now unanimous; the remaining debate in round 2 is the numerator
$\cosh\alpha$ versus $\sinh\alpha$, i.e. the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ over-
constraint versus the independent $u_{x}(0)=0$ kinematic condition.
With the physically independent steady conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the transfer function above is the viscosity
independent steady Stokes sheet response, in agreement with the
derivation of Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 3, 6, 8, 9 and with the $\sinh$
numerator form of Colleagues 1,5,12 up to the conventional phase/sign. ∎
