reflection_text.10:
The steady Stokes mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$\big(D^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}F=0$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-(\mu/k)\big(F'''-k^{2}F'\big)$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big(F''+k^{2}F\big)\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx$ .

On the free top $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and in the
steady state $\dot e=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$. With $z=0$ top,
$z=h$ base

$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $a=0$, $b=-kc$,

$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,

$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$,
$c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, i.e.

$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+h d\cosh\alpha=0$,
$\alpha=kh$,

$d=-c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=2k\big[d\cosh\alpha+d\alpha\sinh\alpha
-k^{2}ch\cosh\alpha\big]
=-\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$.

Hence with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$

$S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\dfrac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]
     =\rho ge\,\dfrac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
       +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},\qquad\alpha=kh,$

the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in
the sign, $e_{s}=-\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ in the sign convention used
above.  The viscosity drops out.  With the isostatic restoring stress
written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$.

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}
/\Delta\rho g$, and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the
usual viscous screening.

The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form quoted by
Colleagues 1,5,12 is the same transfer function up to the conventional
$\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ phase/sign. With the magnitude convention
$e_{s}>0$ for the $\cos kx$ normal stress the magnitude is often written

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
         \dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$
for $\alpha\gg1$.  The $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange is the
$180^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the
$\cos kx$ dynamic topography and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is the
conventional change from the plate density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$ to the isostatic buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$.  The
over-constrained $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ calculation gives the compact
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression above; dropping
the $F(0)=0$ independent condition converts the numerator to the
commonly quoted $\sinh$ form. ∎

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The biharmonic solution is agreed on, so the remaining freedom is how the free-surface conditions are counted. With the harmonic ansatz

$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.

The four physical conditions for the steady mode are

* $u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the material condition is $u_z(0)=0$.
It is the integrated-in-time statement $\dot e=0$ and is not an
independent biharmonic constraint on $F$. The independent kinematic
condition at the free surface is $F'(0)=0$ only. Imposing both
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic constraints over-
constrains the Stokes sheet and removes the $B(z)=-kF(z)$ contribution
to the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that appears in
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

Writing $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $F'(0)=0$ gives $b+kc=0$,
$a$ is irrelevant, and with $F'(0)=0$

$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\Delta\rho g e$,

$c=-\Delta\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives

$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha=kh$,

$d=c\big[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha\big]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\big]$,

and

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =2k\frac{a_{1}}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]
   \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$,

with $a_{1}$ the coefficient of $z\cosh kz$ in the conventional
$\Phi(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz$ notation.
Hence

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}$,

so that in the steady, viscosity independent limit

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(\alpha)$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its
base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.

The numerator is odd in $k$, as required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between basal shear and topography. The long-wave
behaviour is

$\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$,

i.e. $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit
$u_{x}\sim S_{0}z(h-z)/\mu$ with $u_{z}=O(\alpha^{2})$ and zero net
vertical pumping in the steady state. A linear $\chi\simeq\alpha$ long
wave limit would require an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at
the free surface in the steady state, inconsistent with $\dot e=0$.
For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential screening.

With the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ the same algebra gives
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
and the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement in the restoring
stress is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above. The
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form obtained by imposing
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent conditions is the formal
over-constrained result; with the physically distinct free-surface
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, together with
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the transfer function is the
sinh-numerator form above, in agreement with the independent
derivations of Colleagues 1,5 and 12. ∎

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ with $\alpha=kh$ is now essentially settled, so the only remaining physical choice is the hyperbolic function that multiplies $\alpha$ in the numerator.  The difference is not a sign or a $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase, it is the independent kinematic condition that is used at the free surface.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ and
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz .
$$

The physical conditions for the steady dynamic topography are

* kinematic: $u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$,
* dynamic top: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge_{s}\cos kx$,
* free base normal traction: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$,
* imposed basal shear: $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ we have $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $e_{t}=0$, but this is a consequence of the steady state, not an independent biharmonic constraint on $\Phi$.  Imposing $\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic conditions over-constrains the problem and removes the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ contribution to the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that enters $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the independent set $a_{0}=0$, $a_{1}+kb_{0}=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$
a_{1}= \frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\mu}\,e_{s},\qquad b_{0}=-a_{1}/k ,
$$

and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
\Phi'''(h)=-k^{2}\Phi'(h)\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big].
$$

Then

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[a_{1}\sinh kz+b_{1}\cosh kz\big]+\cdots
$$

and the combination that enters the basal shear is

$$
a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh
     =\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\cosh kh\;\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh},
$$

so that with $a_{1}$ above

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =2\mu k\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{\cosh kh}
     \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\; .
$$

Eliminating $a_{1}$,

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh},
$$

i.e. in the steady limit $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \chi(\alpha),\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\,\sinh\alpha}
                 {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its base
and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  The numerator is the odd
$\sinh\alpha$ required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$
basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography, and it comes explicitly from the
$P\propto B''-k^{2}B$ part of $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ with $B=-k\Phi$.

The long-wave limit is the lubrication one,

$$
\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
$$

so $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $e_{s}\to0$ for a very long
wave, as required by $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the steady impermeability $\dot e=0$.
A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$ long-wave limit would require an $O(kh)$
residual vertical velocity at the free surface in the steady state and is
inconsistent with $e_{t}=0$.

For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential viscous screening of short wavelength basal tractions.  The
transfer function is viscosity independent, as it must be for a steady
Stokes sheet.

The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form obtained by
imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic
conditions is the algebraically over-constrained solution.  Formally
replacing $P(0)=-\Delta\rho ge$ with $P(0)=-\rho ge$ and keeping the extra
$\Phi(0)=0$ condition turns the physical $a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh$
contribution into a formal $\cosh$ numerator.  The claim that
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ is a $180^{\circ}$ phase convention is not
correct: phase is $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$, not
$\sinh kh\leftrightarrow\cosh kh$.

With the conventional density contrast $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the steady dynamic topography generated by $S_{0}\sin kx$ is therefore

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which satisfies $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and has the correct quadratic
thin-sheet and exponential thick-sheet limits.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
normalisation is unity in the usual isostatic identification.

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the four independent physical conditions at the top and base are the ones that are actually needed for the steady Stokes sheet, and the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ pair used by Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 4, 8, 9 is an over-constraint. 

With $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

the biharmonic solution is $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.
The free surface can be taken as $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $F'(0)=0$, and the
normal stress jump $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. $P(0)=-\rho g e$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the material condition is $u_{z}(0)=0$,
which is the integrated statement $\dot e=0$, not an independent
kinematic constraint on $F$.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ in addition to $F'(0)=0$ is the double counting that Colleague 1 flags.

Keeping the independent set

* $F'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

gives with the usual $A=0$, $B=-kC$ normalisation
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho g e$, $C=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0
\iff C\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
$$

$\alpha=kh$, whence

$$
d=C\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}.
$$

Then

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[-k^{2}Cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kC}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]\,
   \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha},
$$

the explicit $\sinh\alpha$ coming from the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ part of the
pressure–vertical velocity coupling,
$P\propto B''-k^{2}B$, and from the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation
$P(h)=2\mu kF'(h)$.

Hence

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kC}{h\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]\,
       \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha},
$$

and with $C=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\sinh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

so that with the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
                {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}} .
$$

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is absorbed in the
sign of $e_{s}$; in modulus this is the form Colleague 11 itself notes is
“often written” as the magnitude of the transfer function.

Physically this is the lubrication limit that is required by $u_{x}(0)=0$.
For $\alpha\ll1$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\qquad
e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

so $e_{s}\to0$ for a very long wave, as required by a no-slip horizontal
velocity at the free surface and $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state.  The
linear $\chi\approx\alpha$ long-wave limit obtained with the independent
$F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ pair would require an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical
velocity at the free surface in the steady limit, inconsistent with
$\dot e=0$.

For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential Stokes screening of short wavelength basal tractions.  The
denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now agreed on; the numerator
is the $\sinh\alpha$ coming from the $a_{1}\sinh\alpha+b_{1}\cosh\alpha=
a_{1}\cosh\alpha/kh$ combination after the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ coupling.
Up to the conventional sign/phase the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form quoted by Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 4, 8, 9 is the same
algebra with the extra independent condition $F(0)=0$ imposed and is the
$180^{\circ}$ phase convention of the present expression.  With the usual
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification this is the viscosity-independent
steady dynamic topography $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
sinh-numerator screening factor above, in agreement with Colleagues 1, 5
and 12.

3.text:
With $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base put

$$
\psi =F(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx , \qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

so that $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu }{k}\Big[F'''-k^{2}F'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

and

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$, $e=e_{s}$, the material surface is
$u_{z}(0)=0$ and the only independent kinematic condition at the free
surface is $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
F'(0)=0,\qquad F(0)=0\ {\rm in\ the\ steady\ limit} ,
$$

so that with $\alpha=kh$

$$
F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz ,\qquad
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big] .
$$

The free surface normal stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx
$$

gives

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge ,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho ge}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

Zero normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0
$$

is

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Then

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Hence with the imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $c$ with $c=-\rho ge_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e_{s}\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state, up to the conventional
$180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
             \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}.
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  Writing the
isostatic restoring traction at the free surface as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional dynamic
topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
            \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
                  \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
       =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
             \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

with the $180^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto-\sin kx$ for the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal traction.  In modulus form this is often quoted as

$$
|e_{s}|=
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase convention.  In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
Stokes screening $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  Restoring the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation the viscosity independent steady
response to the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$ is
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ above, which for
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ reduces to the familiar $[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+
\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ sheet screening factor.  The $\sinh$ numerator
form is the same expression up to the conventional sign/phase absorbed
in the definition of $e_{s}$. ∎

4.text:
With $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base put

$$
\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx,
\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

so that

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}F=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\!\left[F'''-k^{2}F'\right], 
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\!\left[F''+k^{2}F\right]\sin kx ,\qquad

$$

In the steady material state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is material

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=\dot e =0,
$$

i.e.

$$
F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,
$$

and with $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

$F(0)=F'(0)=0$ gives $a=0,\;b=-kc$ and

$$
F(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
P(z)=2\mu k\Big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\Big],\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c .
$$

The imposed normal stress on the deflected top is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx,
$$

hence

$$
P(0)=-\rho ge,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho ge}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

Zero normal traction at the base,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

so that

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
$$

Now

$$
F''+k^{2}F
=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx,
$$

i.e.

$$
S_{0}=-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
      \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $c$ with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}, 
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

so that in the $t\to\infty$ steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the minus sign being the $180^{o}$ phase between the imposed
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.  The
viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  In modulus

$$
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
       =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
\chi_{\rho}\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\quad\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{\rho}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\quad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ for long waves and exponential
viscous screening for $kh\gg1$.

Writing the restoring stress in the conventional isostatic form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the dynamic topography is
conventionally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}
             \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
                  +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
                  +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the sign being absorbed in the definition of $e_{s}$.  In magnitude
the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase convention is
often written as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer
function up to the $180^{o}$ $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase.  With
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ this is the viscosity-independent steady Stokes sheet
transfer function $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ generated by the
harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor is unity for the usual isostatic identification and the
$kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form is the
$[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ screening factor quoted
in the literature. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ with $\alpha=kh$ is now essentially settled and the only remaining freedom is the numerator and the way the free-surface kinematics is imposed.  Writing with $z=0$ at the free top and $z=h$ at the base

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ gives 
$\Phi=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$.  The independent kinematic condition at the free surface is $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'(0)=0$.  The condition $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, is the integrated-in-time statement $\dot e=0$ and is not an independent biharmonic constraint on $\Phi$; imposing it together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ over-constrains the four constants and is the source of the formal $\cosh$ numerator.

Keeping the four physical conditions

* $\Phi'(0)=0$, 
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, 
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

we may put $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=C\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Dz\sinh kz,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k^{2}C\cosh kz-2\mu kD\sinh kz,
$$

with $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho g e$, i.e. 
$C=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  The zero normal traction at the base gives

$$
C\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+Dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad D=C\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha},
\qquad \alpha=kh .
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-k^{2}Cz\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that at $z=h$

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
 =2k\,C\frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}.
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =\frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
       \Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big],
$$

i.e. in the steady state

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}} .
$$

With the isostatic restoring stress written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional dynamic-topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
\qquad \alpha=kh,
$$

up to the inessential $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase.  In modulus this is the form most often quoted as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

The numerator is odd in $k$, as required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography, and the long-wave behaviour is

$$
\chi\simeq \alpha^{2}\big[1+O(\alpha^{2})\big],\qquad \alpha\ll1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a very long wave.  This is the lubrication expectation for a sheet with $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$: the vertical pumping is $u_{z}\sim k\Phi\sim O((kh)^{2})$ and a linear $kh$ long-wave limit would require a residual $O(kh)$ vertical velocity at the free surface, incompatible with the steady material surface condition.  For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim \alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar exponential viscous screening of short wavelength basal tractions.

Imposing the additional independent condition $\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ converts the combination $a_{1}\sinh\alpha+b_{1}\cosh\alpha=a_{1}\cosh\alpha/kh$ that follows from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ into the formal $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression.  That is the $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign convention discussed by Colleagues 10,11,2,4,6,8,9, i.e. the same transfer function up to $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ with the sign absorbed in $e_{s}$.  Keeping the physically distinct free-surface conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the independent kinematic condition is $\Phi'(0)=0$ and the steady amplitude is the $\sinh$-numerator form above, viscosity independent, with the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation explicit in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

9.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx , \qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$ gives with $z=0$ the free top and $z=h$
the base

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$,

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,
$$

i.e. $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big].
$$

The free surface normal stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx
$$

gives

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e,\qquad
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},
$$

and the zero normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
$$

gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0 ,
\qquad \alpha\equiv kh ,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
$$

Hence

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi =2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
$$

and

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\,\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
$$

is therefore

$$
S_{0}=-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]
      =\frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

In the time independent limit $e=e_{s}$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
      \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the $-$ sign being the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase between the basal traction and the topography.  With the
isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the viscosity independent
dynamic–topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

so that for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  The viscosity drops out of the
steady amplitude.  Up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign the
magnitude is often quoted as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase convention.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi^{-1}= \alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha$, the familiar
viscosity independent Stokes sheet screening factor.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor is unity for the conventional isostatic replacement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$. ∎

2.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx ,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx
$$

$$
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}F=0,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[F'''-k^{2}F'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]\sin kx,
\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu kF'\Big]\cos kx,
$$

and $z=0$ at the free surface, $z=h$ at the base.  In the $t\to\infty$
steady state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is material so that

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0,\;\;F(0)=0,
$$

together with

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx .
\end{equation*}
With
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ the two kinematic conditions give
$a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$$
F(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz,
$$
$$
P(z)=2\mu k\Big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\Big],\qquad P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c .
$$

Hence

$$
P(0)=-\rho g e\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
P(0)=-\rho g e .
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, i.e.

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

so that

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Now

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}
      =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big].
$$

Hence

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}
      =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
        \Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big]=S_{0},
$$

and with $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
S_{0}= \frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big],
$$

i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
             +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the minus sign being the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase between the imposed basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.
The amplitude is viscosity independent.  Putting the isostatic restoring
stress in the form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional
dynamic-topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

so that with the $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
        \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
              +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh .
$$

For the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
      +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
Stokes screening $e_{s}\propto kh\,e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh\gg1$.  With the sign absorbed in the definition of $e_{s}$ the
magnitude is conventionally quoted as

$$
\big|e_{s}\big|
   =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
     \frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $180^{\circ}$ phase convention.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ and the
transfer function is viscosity independent.  This is the
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
Stokes sheet response, $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, with the
linear $kh$ long-wave limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
exponential short-wave screening normally quoted in the literature. ∎

public_text.5:
The biharmonic solution is agreed on, so the remaining freedom is how the free-surface conditions are counted. With the harmonic ansatz

$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.

The four physical conditions for the steady mode are

* $u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the material condition is $u_z(0)=0$.
It is the integrated-in-time statement $\dot e=0$ and is not an
independent biharmonic constraint on $F$. The independent kinematic
condition at the free surface is $F'(0)=0$ only. Imposing both
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic constraints over-
constrains the Stokes sheet and removes the $B(z)=-kF(z)$ contribution
to the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that appears in
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

Writing $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $F'(0)=0$ gives $b+kc=0$,
$a$ is irrelevant, and with $F'(0)=0$

$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\Delta\rho g e$,

$c=-\Delta\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives

$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha=kh$,

$d=c\big[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha\big]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\big]$,

and

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =2k\frac{a_{1}}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]
   \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$,

with $a_{1}$ the coefficient of $z\cosh kz$ in the conventional
$\Phi(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz$ notation.
Hence

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
\frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}$,

so that in the steady, viscosity independent limit

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi(\alpha)$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its
base and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.

The numerator is odd in $k$, as required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between basal shear and topography. The long-wave
behaviour is

$\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$,

i.e. $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit
$u_{x}\sim S_{0}z(h-z)/\mu$ with $u_{z}=O(\alpha^{2})$ and zero net
vertical pumping in the steady state. A linear $\chi\simeq\alpha$ long
wave limit would require an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at
the free surface in the steady state, inconsistent with $\dot e=0$.
For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential screening.

With the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ the same algebra gives
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\,\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
and the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement in the restoring
stress is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\chi$ above. The
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form obtained by imposing
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent conditions is the formal
over-constrained result; with the physically distinct free-surface
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, together with
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the transfer function is the
sinh-numerator form above, in agreement with the independent
derivations of Colleagues 1,5 and 12. ∎

* kinematic: $u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$,
* dynamic top: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge_{s}\cos kx$,
* free base normal traction: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$,
* imposed basal shear: $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ we have $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $e_{t}=0$, but this is a consequence of the steady state, not an independent biharmonic constraint on $\Phi$.  Imposing $\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic conditions over-constrains the problem and removes the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ contribution to the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that enters $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the independent set $a_{0}=0$, $a_{1}+kb_{0}=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$
a_{1}= \frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\mu}\,e_{s},\qquad b_{0}=-a_{1}/k ,
$$

and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
\Phi'''(h)=-k^{2}\Phi'(h)\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big].
$$

Then

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[a_{1}\sinh kz+b_{1}\cosh kz\big]+\cdots
$$

and the combination that enters the basal shear is

$$
a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh
     =\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\cosh kh\;\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh},
$$

so that with $a_{1}$ above

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =2\mu k\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{\cosh kh}
     \frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh}\; .
$$

Eliminating $a_{1}$,

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
       \frac{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}{kh\,\sinh kh},
$$

i.e. in the steady limit $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \chi(\alpha),\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\,\sinh\alpha}
                 {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the usual Stokes screening factor for a viscous sheet forced at its base
and free at its top with $u_{x}(0)=0$.  The numerator is the odd
$\sinh\alpha$ required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$
basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography, and it comes explicitly from the
$P\propto B''-k^{2}B$ part of $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ with $B=-k\Phi$.

The long-wave limit is the lubrication one,

$$
\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
$$

so $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $e_{s}\to0$ for a very long
wave, as required by $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the steady impermeability $\dot e=0$.
A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$ long-wave limit would require an $O(kh)$
residual vertical velocity at the free surface in the steady state and is
inconsistent with $e_{t}=0$.

For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential viscous screening of short wavelength basal tractions.  The
transfer function is viscosity independent, as it must be for a steady
Stokes sheet.

The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form obtained by
imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic
conditions is the algebraically over-constrained solution.  Formally
replacing $P(0)=-\Delta\rho ge$ with $P(0)=-\rho ge$ and keeping the extra
$\Phi(0)=0$ condition turns the physical $a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh$
contribution into a formal $\cosh$ numerator.  The claim that
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ is a $180^{\circ}$ phase convention is not
correct: phase is $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$, not
$\sinh kh\leftrightarrow\cosh kh$.

With the conventional density contrast $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the steady dynamic topography generated by $S_{0}\sin kx$ is therefore

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which satisfies $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and has the correct quadratic
thin-sheet and exponential thick-sheet limits.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
normalisation is unity in the usual isostatic identification.
public_text.12:
I think the four independent physical conditions at the top and base are the ones that are actually needed for the steady Stokes sheet, and the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ pair used by Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 4, 8, 9 is an over-constraint. 

With $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

the biharmonic solution is $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.
The free surface can be taken as $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $F'(0)=0$, and the
normal stress jump $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. $P(0)=-\rho g e$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the material condition is $u_{z}(0)=0$,
which is the integrated statement $\dot e=0$, not an independent
kinematic constraint on $F$.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ in addition to $F'(0)=0$ is the double counting that Colleague 1 flags.

Keeping the independent set

* $F'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

gives with the usual $A=0$, $B=-kC$ normalisation
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho g e$, $C=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0
\iff C\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
$$

$\alpha=kh$, whence

$$
d=C\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}.
$$

Then

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[-k^{2}Cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kC}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]\,
   \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha},
$$

the explicit $\sinh\alpha$ coming from the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ part of the
pressure–vertical velocity coupling,
$P\propto B''-k^{2}B$, and from the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ relation
$P(h)=2\mu kF'(h)$.

Hence

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kC}{h\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]\,
       \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha},
$$

and with $C=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\sinh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

so that with the isostatic restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
                {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}} .
$$

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is absorbed in the
sign of $e_{s}$; in modulus this is the form Colleague 11 itself notes is
“often written” as the magnitude of the transfer function.

Physically this is the lubrication limit that is required by $u_{x}(0)=0$.
For $\alpha\ll1$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\qquad
e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

so $e_{s}\to0$ for a very long wave, as required by a no-slip horizontal
velocity at the free surface and $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state.  The
linear $\chi\approx\alpha$ long-wave limit obtained with the independent
$F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ pair would require an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical
velocity at the free surface in the steady limit, inconsistent with
$\dot e=0$.

For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential Stokes screening of short wavelength basal tractions.  The
denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now agreed on; the numerator
is the $\sinh\alpha$ coming from the $a_{1}\sinh\alpha+b_{1}\cosh\alpha=
a_{1}\cosh\alpha/kh$ combination after the $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ coupling.
Up to the conventional sign/phase the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form quoted by Colleagues 10, 11, 2, 4, 8, 9 is the same
algebra with the extra independent condition $F(0)=0$ imposed and is the
$180^{\circ}$ phase convention of the present expression.  With the usual
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification this is the viscosity-independent
steady dynamic topography $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the
sinh-numerator screening factor above, in agreement with Colleagues 1, 5
and 12.

With $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base put

$$
\psi =F(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx , \qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

so that $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu }{k}\Big[F'''-k^{2}F'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

and

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$, $e=e_{s}$, the material surface is
$u_{z}(0)=0$ and the only independent kinematic condition at the free
surface is $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
F'(0)=0,\qquad F(0)=0\ {\rm in\ the\ steady\ limit} ,
$$

so that with $\alpha=kh$

$$
F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz ,\qquad
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big] .
$$

The free surface normal stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx
$$

gives

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge ,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho ge}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

Zero normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0
$$

is

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Then

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Hence with the imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $c$ with $c=-\rho ge_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e_{s}\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ steady state, up to the conventional
$180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
             \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}.
$$

The viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  Writing the
isostatic restoring traction at the free surface as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional dynamic
topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
            \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
                  \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
       =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+
             \frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

with the $180^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto-\sin kx$ for the
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal traction.  In modulus form this is often quoted as

$$
|e_{s}|=
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase convention.  In particular

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
Stokes screening $\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}$ for $kh\gg1$.  Restoring the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation the viscosity independent steady
response to the harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$ is
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ above, which for
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ reduces to the familiar $[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+
\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ sheet screening factor.  The $\sinh$ numerator
form is the same expression up to the conventional sign/phase absorbed
in the definition of $e_{s}$. ∎

With $z=0$ at the free surface and $z=h$ at the base put

$$
\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx,
\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

so that

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}F=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\!\left[F'''-k^{2}F'\right], 
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\!\left[F''+k^{2}F\right]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu kF'\Big]\cos kx .
$$

In the steady material state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is material

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=\dot e =0,
$$

i.e.

$$
F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,
$$

and with $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

$F(0)=F'(0)=0$ gives $a=0,\;b=-kc$ and

$$
F(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
P(z)=2\mu k\Big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\Big],\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c .
$$

The imposed normal stress on the deflected top is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx,
$$

hence

$$
P(0)=-\rho ge,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho ge}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

Zero normal traction at the base,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

so that

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
$$

Now

$$
F''+k^{2}F
=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx,
$$

i.e.

$$
S_{0}=-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
      \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $c$ with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}, 
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

so that in the $t\to\infty$ steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the minus sign being the $180^{o}$ phase between the imposed
$S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.  The
viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  In modulus

$$
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
       =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
\chi_{\rho}\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\quad\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi_{\rho}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\quad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$ for long waves and exponential
viscous screening for $kh\gg1$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the dynamic topography is
conventionally quoted as

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}
             \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
                  +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
           =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
                  +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the sign being absorbed in the definition of $e_{s}$.  In magnitude
the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase convention is
often written as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

function up to the $180^{o}$ $\sin\!\leftrightarrow\!\cos$ phase.  With
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ this is the viscosity-independent steady Stokes sheet
transfer function $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ generated by the
harmonic basal shear $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor is unity for the usual isostatic identification and the
$kh\cosh kh/[(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form is the
$[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ screening factor quoted
in the literature. ∎

The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ with $\alpha=kh$ is now essentially settled and the only remaining freedom is the numerator and the way the free-surface kinematics is imposed.  Writing with $z=0$ at the free top and $z=h$ at the base

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ gives 
$\Phi=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.
In the steady state $\dot e=0$.  The independent kinematic condition at the free surface is $u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'(0)=0$.  The condition $u_{z}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$, is the integrated-in-time statement $\dot e=0$ and is not an independent biharmonic constraint on $\Phi$; imposing it together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ over-constrains the four constants and is the source of the formal $\cosh$ numerator.

Keeping the four physical conditions

* $\Phi'(0)=0$, 
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, 
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

we may put $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=C\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Dz\sinh kz,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k^{2}C\cosh kz-2\mu kD\sinh kz,
$$

with $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}C=-\rho g e$, i.e. 
$C=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  The zero normal traction at the base gives

$$
C\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+Dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad D=C\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha},
\qquad \alpha=kh .
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-k^{2}Cz\cosh kz+D\cosh kz+Dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that at $z=h$

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
 =2k\,C\frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}.
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
     =\frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
       \Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big],
$$

i.e. in the steady state

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}} .
$$

With the isostatic restoring stress written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional dynamic-topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
\qquad \alpha=kh,
$$

up to the inessential $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase.  In modulus this is the form most often quoted as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}} .
$$

The numerator is odd in $k$, as required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the $\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography, and the long-wave behaviour is

$$
\chi\simeq \alpha^{2}\big[1+O(\alpha^{2})\big],\qquad \alpha\ll1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\propto (kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a very long wave.  This is the lubrication expectation for a sheet with $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$: the vertical pumping is $u_{z}\sim k\Phi\sim O((kh)^{2})$ and a linear $kh$ long-wave limit would require a residual $O(kh)$ vertical velocity at the free surface, incompatible with the steady material surface condition.  For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim \alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar exponential viscous screening of short wavelength basal tractions.

Imposing the additional independent condition $\Phi(0)=0$ together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ converts the combination $a_{1}\sinh\alpha+b_{1}\cosh\alpha=a_{1}\cosh\alpha/kh$ that follows from $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ into the formal $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression.  That is the $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign convention discussed by Colleagues 10,11,2,4,6,8,9, i.e. the same transfer function up to $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ with the sign absorbed in $e_{s}$.  Keeping the physically distinct free-surface conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, the independent kinematic condition is $\Phi'(0)=0$ and the steady amplitude is the $\sinh$-numerator form above, viscosity independent, with the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation explicit in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎
public_text.9:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx , \qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi =0$ gives with $z=0$ the free top and $z=h$
the base

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$,

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,
$$

i.e. $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$$
\Phi(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big].
$$

The free surface normal stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx
$$

gives

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e,\qquad
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},
$$

and the zero normal traction at the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
$$

gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0 ,
\qquad \alpha\equiv kh ,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha} .
$$

Hence

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi =2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big]
$$

and

$$
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\,\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}=S_{0}\sin kx
$$

is therefore

$$
S_{0}=-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]
      =\frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

In the time independent limit $e=e_{s}$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
      \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the $-$ sign being the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase between the basal traction and the topography.  With the
isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the viscosity independent
dynamic–topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

so that for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  The viscosity drops out of the
steady amplitude.  Up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign the
magnitude is often quoted as

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase convention.  With $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
this is $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi^{-1}= \alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha$, the familiar
viscosity independent Stokes sheet screening factor.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor is unity for the conventional isostatic replacement
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$. ∎
public_text.2:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx ,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx
$$

$$
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}F=0,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[F'''-k^{2}F'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]\sin kx,
\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu kF'\Big]\cos kx,
$$

and $z=0$ at the free surface, $z=h$ at the base.  In the $t\to\infty$
steady state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is material so that

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad u_{z}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0,\;\;F(0)=0,
$$

together with

\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx .
\end{equation*}
With
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ the two kinematic conditions give
$a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$$
F(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz,
$$
$$
P(z)=2\mu k\Big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\Big],\qquad P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c .
$$

Hence

$$
P(0)=-\rho g e\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad 
P(0)=-\rho g e .
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, i.e.

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

so that

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Now

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}
      =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big].
$$

Hence

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}
      =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
        \Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big]=S_{0},
$$

and with $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
S_{0}= \frac{\rho g e}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
       \Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big],
$$

i.e. in the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
             +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

the minus sign being the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase between the imposed basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.
The amplitude is viscosity independent.  Putting the isostatic restoring
stress in the form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional
dynamic-topography transfer function is

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

so that with the $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
        \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
              +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh .
$$

For the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
      +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
$$

so that

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\gg1,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
Stokes screening $e_{s}\propto kh\,e^{-kh}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh\gg1$.  With the sign absorbed in the definition of $e_{s}$ the
magnitude is conventionally quoted as

$$
\big|e_{s}\big|
   =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
     \frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $180^{\circ}$ phase convention.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ and the
transfer function is viscosity independent.  This is the
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
Stokes sheet response, $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, with the
linear $kh$ long-wave limit $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and the
exponential short-wave screening normally quoted in the literature. ∎

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic sheet with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$.
Denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$, is now essentially settled and viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude.

The dispute is the independent set of free-surface conditions. The statement gives at $z=0$
$u_x=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e(t)\cos kx$, and at $z=h$
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$. The material surface condition is
$u_z(0)=\dot e$, i.e. $-k\Phi(0)=\dot e$. In the time dependent problem $\Phi(0)\neq0$ is allowed and $e(t)$ evolves. In the steady limit $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0$ as a consequence, not an independent biharmonic constraint. Imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the two stress conditions over-constrains the four constants and removes the $B(z)=-k\Phi$ contribution to the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that enters $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the physically independent set $\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ one may put $a=0$, $b=-kc$, 
$a_{1}=b$, 
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz]$ and
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2k a_{1}h^{-1}\cosh^{-1}\alpha[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]\sinh\alpha/\cosh\alpha$.
Eliminating $a_{1}$ with $P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=-\rho g e$ gives
$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\sinh\alpha]$,
hence in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\; \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, 
$\alpha=kh$,

up to the conventional $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign. The
viscosity drops out. With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional transfer function is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(\alpha)=\rho/\Delta\rho\; \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,

and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
Long wave $\alpha\ll1$: $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, i.e.
$e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit with a no-slip
horizontal velocity at the free surface and $\dot e=0$, and
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar exponential Stokes screening.

If the extra independent biharmonic condition $\Phi(0)=0$ is imposed together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ the formal over-constrained solution is obtained. With $a=0$, $b=-kc$, $\Phi(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$ one gets
$S_{0}= \rho g e[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$,
i.e.

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\; \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
      =S_{0}/\rho g\,[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,

so that with the $\Delta\rho$ normalisation
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\rho/\Delta\rho\,\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$.
For $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the often quoted $[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ screening factor, $\chi\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$. The $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange is the $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase/sign convention; in modulus the two forms are commonly written as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\; \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$

with the over-constrained $\alpha\cosh\alpha$ form the same up to sign.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ and viscosity independence are agreed; the remaining open issue is the physically correct counting of free-surface conditions, i.e. $\sinh$ numerator with $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ long wave versus the formal $\cosh$ numerator with $\chi\sim\alpha$ long wave obtained by imposing $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic constraints. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes sheet is now settled on the biharmonic form
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, in the notation
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$. The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$, is agreed on.

The remaining split is the independent free-surface conditions.  The
physical set for the deflected layer is
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  In the steady material
limit $e_{t}=0$ one has $u_{z}(0)=0\iff F(0)=0$, but $F(0)=0$ is the
integrated-in-time consequence of $e_{t}=0$ and is not an independent
biharmonic constraint on $F$.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ together with $F'(0)=0$
as two independent biharmonic conditions over-constrains the sheet and
removes the $B=-kF$ pressure–vertical-velocity coupling in
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the independent set $F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ one has $a=0$, $b+ k c=0$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -\frac{2k c}{h\cosh\alpha}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$,

so that

$S_{0}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ $\dot e=0$ limit

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$, $\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is the conventional
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with, up to the usual $180^{\circ}$
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase,

$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$, and
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.  Hence
$e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a very long wave and
exponential Stokes screening for $kh\gg1$, as required by $u_{x}(0)=0$
and $\dot e=0$.

The $180^{\circ}$ phase is often absorbed and the transfer function is
quoted in magnitude as the $\cosh$-numerator form

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
=[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,

i.e. $|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,
\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, which is the same
algebraic screening factor up to $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ and sign.
Imposing the extra independent condition $F(0)=0$ together with
$F'(0)=0$ gives the formal over-constrained solution
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
with the linear long-wave limit $\chi\simeq\alpha$.  That linear limit
requires an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at the free surface in
the steady state and is inconsistent with $e_{t}=0$ when $F'(0)=0$ is the
only independent kinematic condition.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation
is inessential; with the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the
conversion to $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor
$\Delta\rho/\rho$.  Up to the conventional sign/phase this is the
viscosity-independent steady dynamic-topography transfer function for a
viscous sheet forced at its base by $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎

$$

state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is impermeable, $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$.

undetermined additive constant of $\psi$.  With $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$

$a=0$, $b=-kc$, 
$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$,

\iff V_{h}\cosh\alpha+U_{h}\sinh\alpha=0$, $U_{h}=a+bh$, $V_{h}=c+dh$,

and

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big].
$$

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =\rho g e\,\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},

\qquad\alpha=kh,

{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},

$$

{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$

\qquad

{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
