rather than an independent biharmonic constraint.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ and
$F'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic conditions is the physical
steady-state gauge and leads to the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function above, $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential Stokes screening for $kh\gg1$,
with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation explicit in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The
viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude. ∎

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives

$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $z=0$ free, $z=h$ base.
The physically independent steady conditions are

$u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, and in the steady
material state $\dot e=0\iff u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0$.  With
$a=0$, $b+ k c=0$

$\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$,

$c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, 
$\alpha=kh$,

$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\big]$

and

$\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$.

Hence

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
      =-\dfrac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]
      =S_{0}$,

i.e. with $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,\dfrac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

so in the $t\to\infty$ limit

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
          +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  The steady material condition
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is required for a unique solution; the four
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ are three equations for $c,d,e$ and $a=0$ fixes
the rigid translation.  The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ is now
unanimous.

Writing the restoring stress at the free surface in the conventional
isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
$\alpha=kh$, and for the usual geophysical identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\;\;e_{s}\simeq \dfrac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase between the
imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography is
normally absorbed in the sign.  In modulus form this is conventionally
quoted as

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

i.e. $|\chi_{m}|\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$|\chi_{m}|\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual sign/phase
convention.  The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
form is the linear long-wave limit $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
required by $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state; the
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ magnitude is the same
transfer function up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ phase.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is unity for the usual isostatic
replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  This is the viscosity independent
steady Stokes sheet screening to a harmonic basal traction. ∎

6.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ gives

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

and with $z=0$ the top and $z=h$ the base

$$
\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-\,P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx ,
$$

in the steady material state $e_{t}=u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$,
$a=0$, $b=-kc$, and

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big] .
\end{equation*}
Hence

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge ,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho ge}{2\mu k^{2}} ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff 
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha},
$$

and

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big].
$$

At $z=h$

\[
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big],
\]

so that with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$

\[
S_{0}=-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]
     =\rho g\,e\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh .
\]

In the $t\to\infty$ limit $e_{t}=0$ the amplitude of the material
topography is therefore, up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ 
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

\[
e_{s}=\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
      \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
    =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

and the viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  Writing the
isostatic restoring stress at the free surface in the conventional form

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho\,g\,e\cos kx ,
\]

the viscosity independent Stokes sheet transfer function may be written
as

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
           +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

i.e.

\[
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

so that for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

\[
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

\[
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big((kh)^{3}\big),\;\;kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi(kh)\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\;\;kh\gg1,
\]

the familiar viscous Stokes screening.  In modulus form the
$180^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and
the $\cos kx$ topography is often absorbed and the transfer function is
quoted as

\[
\big|e_{s}\big|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

i.e. $ |e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/
\alpha]^{-1}$ up to sign, 
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$.  With the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation restored this is the
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ Stokes sheet response; for
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ the signed transfer function is the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form above, whose
modulus is the often quoted $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}
\alpha]$ screening factor.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity in the
usual isostatic convention.  This is the viscosity independent steady
dynamic topography generated by the harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$. ∎

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream function $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $P=-(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.  With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base

$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$.

The four physical Stokes conditions are

$u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,
and the kinematic condition $u_z(0)=\dot e$, $u_z(0)=-kF(0)\cos kx$.
For the quasi-static problem $F$ is slaved to $e(t)$ and the
evolution is $\dot e=-kF(0)$.  In the $t\to\infty$ material steady
state $\dot e=0$ so that $F(0)=0$ and the steady mode can be written
with $a=0$, $b=-kc$ as

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,

$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$, 
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$, $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ i.e.

$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+h d\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha\equiv kh$,

$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$
and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$.

Hence in the $t\to\infty$ viscous steady state, viscosity independent,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

the minus sign being the $180^{o}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase.  Writing the restoring stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the conventional isostatic transfer function is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$,

$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}
 =\big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.
The viscosity drops out.

The $180^{o}$ phase is conventionally absorbed in the definition of
$e_{s}>0$ and the magnitude is often quoted as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha\gg1$,
i.e. the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer
function up to the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign/phase.  With the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation the same
expression is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Imposing $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic conditions
gives the $\alpha\cosh\alpha$ numerator; keeping only the independent
kinematic condition $F'(0)=0$ and treating $F(0)=-\dot e/k$ as the
evolution variable gives the commonly quoted magnitude
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.  The denominator
$\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now settled.  The remaining
difference is the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ $180^{o}$ phase/sign
convention and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation between the plate
density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ and the isostatic
buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ used in $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$ and
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.
The physical steady set is
$u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$
and the material free surface in the steady limit $e_t=0$
$u_z(0)=0\iff F(0)=0$.  With $a=0,\;b+ k c=0$
\[
F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz,\qquad
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big],
\]
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$ so $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives 
$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, 
$\alpha=kh$, and
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then
\[
F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[d\cosh kz+d k z\sinh kz-c k^{2}z\cosh kz\big],
\]
\[
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=2k\Big[d\cosh\alpha+d\alpha\sinh\alpha
-c k\alpha\cosh\alpha\Big]
 =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big].
\]
Hence
\[
S_{0}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big],
\]
and with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$
\[
S_{0}= \rho g e\,\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
\qquad
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\quad\alpha=kh .
\]
The viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude.  Writing the restoring
stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
\[
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha),
\]
and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
\[
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]
so that $\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar viscous
Stokes screening.  The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase
is normally absorbed in the sign; in modulus form this is often quoted as
$\chi_{m}= \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the conventional
sign/phase convention.

The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ numerator with
$\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ is obtained if $F(0)=0$ is not
imposed as an independent biharmonic condition.  With the independent set
$F'(0)=0,\;\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e,\;\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
the system is under-determined and the steady kinematic condition
$F(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=e_{t}=0$, is required to close the problem. Imposing
both $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic constraints as done
by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 gives the transfer function above; the
formal over-constrained solution quoted by Colleagues 1,5,7,12 is the same
transfer function up to the conventional sign/phase and the extra
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation is unity for the usual isostatic
identification.  The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now
unanimous, the remaining difference is the $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ numerator
which is a sign/phase/magnitude convention in the steady material limit.
Viscosity drops out, the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is explicit, and the
long-wave $kh$ and exponential short-wave limits are as above. ∎

The biharmonic sheet with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, 
$\Phi=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$.
Denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$, is now essentially settled and viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude.

The dispute is the independent set of free-surface conditions. The statement gives at $z=0$
$u_x=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e(t)\cos kx$, and at $z=h$
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$. The material surface condition is
$u_z(0)=\dot e$, i.e. $-k\Phi(0)=\dot e$. In the time dependent problem $\Phi(0)\neq0$ is allowed and $e(t)$ evolves. In the steady limit $\dot e=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0$ as a consequence, not an independent biharmonic constraint. Imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ together with the two stress conditions over-constrains the four constants and removes the $B(z)=-k\Phi$ contribution to the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that enters $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the physically independent set $\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ one may put $a=0$, $b=-kc$, 
$a_{1}=b$, 
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz]$ and
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=2k a_{1}h^{-1}\cosh^{-1}\alpha[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]\sinh\alpha/\cosh\alpha$.
Eliminating $a_{1}$ with $P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=-\rho g e$ gives
$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\sinh\alpha]$,
hence in the $t\to\infty$ steady state

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\; \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, 
$\alpha=kh$,

up to the conventional $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign. The
viscosity drops out. With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional transfer function is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(\alpha)=\rho/\Delta\rho\; \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,

and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
Long wave $\alpha\ll1$: $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, i.e.
$e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit with a no-slip
horizontal velocity at the free surface and $\dot e=0$, and
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar exponential Stokes screening.

If the extra independent biharmonic condition $\Phi(0)=0$ is imposed together with $\Phi'(0)=0$ the formal over-constrained solution is obtained. With $a=0$, $b=-kc$, $\Phi(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$ one gets
$S_{0}= \rho g e[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$,
i.e.

$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\; \alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
      =S_{0}/\rho g\,[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,

so that with the $\Delta\rho$ normalisation
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\rho/\Delta\rho\,\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$.
For $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the often quoted $[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ screening factor, $\chi\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$. The $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange is the $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase/sign convention; in modulus the two forms are commonly written as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\; \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$

with the over-constrained $\alpha\cosh\alpha$ form the same up to sign.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ and viscosity independence are agreed; the remaining open issue is the physically correct counting of free-surface conditions, i.e. $\sinh$ numerator with $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ long wave versus the formal $\cosh$ numerator with $\chi\sim\alpha$ long wave obtained by imposing $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic constraints. ∎

reflection_text.2:
The harmonic Stokes sheet is now settled on the biharmonic form
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, in the notation
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$. The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$, is agreed on.

The remaining split is the independent free-surface conditions.  The
physical set for the deflected layer is
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  In the steady material
limit $e_{t}=0$ one has $u_{z}(0)=0\iff F(0)=0$, but $F(0)=0$ is the
integrated-in-time consequence of $e_{t}=0$ and is not an independent
biharmonic constraint on $F$.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ together with $F'(0)=0$
as two independent biharmonic conditions over-constrains the sheet and
removes the $B=-kF$ pressure–vertical-velocity coupling in
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the independent set $F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ one has $a=0$, $b+ k c=0$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -\frac{2k c}{h\cosh\alpha}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$,

so that

$S_{0}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ $\dot e=0$ limit

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$, $\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress written as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is the conventional
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with, up to the usual $180^{\circ}$
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase,

$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$, and
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.  Hence
$e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for a very long wave and
exponential Stokes screening for $kh\gg1$, as required by $u_{x}(0)=0$
and $\dot e=0$.

The $180^{\circ}$ phase is often absorbed and the transfer function is
quoted in magnitude as the $\cosh$-numerator form

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
=[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,

i.e. $|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,
\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, which is the same
algebraic screening factor up to $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ and sign.
Imposing the extra independent condition $F(0)=0$ together with
$F'(0)=0$ gives the formal over-constrained solution
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
with the linear long-wave limit $\chi\simeq\alpha$.  That linear limit
requires an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at the free surface in
the steady state and is inconsistent with $e_{t}=0$ when $F'(0)=0$ is the
only independent kinematic condition.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation
is inessential; with the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the
conversion to $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor
$\Delta\rho/\rho$.  Up to the conventional sign/phase this is the
viscosity-independent steady dynamic-topography transfer function for a
viscous sheet forced at its base by $S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The biharmonic stream function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, 
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,  
$P=-(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$,
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ is now agreed on.

With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base the four physical conditions are
$u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
The material free surface gives $\dot e=u_z(0)=-kF(0)\cos kx$ so that
in the steady limit $\dot e=0$ the kinematic condition $F(0)=0$ is
required.  With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ one may set $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$,
$c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$\alpha=kh$, $d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then
$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=-2kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$ and

$S_{0}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. up to the $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign

$e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
 +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
and for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ identification
$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$\alpha\ll1$ and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.

The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now essentially settled.
The remaining disagreement is the numerator.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ and
$F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic constraints, i.e. the $t\to\infty$
material condition $u_{z}(0)=0$, gives the $\alpha\cosh\alpha$ numerator
above, linear long-wave limit $\chi\sim\alpha$, quoted by Colleagues
10,2,3,4,6,8,9.  Dropping the independent $F(0)=0$ constraint and keeping
only the four physical conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
gives the conventional magnitude form

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$, quoted by Colleagues 1,5,12
and as the magnitude by Colleague 11.  The two forms differ only by the
conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $180^{\circ}$ phase/sign and
by whether the steady kinematic condition $F(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=0$, is
imposed independently.  With the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation is explicit; for $\rho=\Delta\rho$
it is unity.  The viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude and the
exponential Stokes screening for $kh\gg1$ is common to both conventions.
reflection_text.11:
The biharmonic sheet is now settled. With $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx .
$$

The four physical conditions are $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  In the material steady
state $\dot e=0$ the free surface is impermeable, $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$.
That is a genuine gauge condition for the stream function; $F(0)=0$ together
with $F'(0)=0$ fixes the four constants $a,b,c,d$ and removes the
undetermined additive constant of $\psi$.  With $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$

$a=0$, $b=-kc$, 
$F(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$,

$c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)
\iff V_{h}\cosh\alpha+U_{h}\sinh\alpha=0$, $U_{h}=a+bh$, $V_{h}=c+dh$,
$\alpha=kh$.  With $a=0$ this gives $d=c\big[\alpha\tanh\alpha-1\big]/h$
and

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big].
$$

Hence 
$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =\rho g e\,\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
$$
so that in the $t\to\infty$ material steady state

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

viscosity independent.  Writing the restoring traction at the free surface
in the conventional isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$\chi\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.  The $180^{\circ}$
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is normally absorbed in the sign, so
the magnitude often quoted is

$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the conventional sign/
phase convention.  The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now
essentially agreed on.  

The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form with the
quadratic long-wave limit $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}$ obtained by Colleagues 1,
5, 12 corresponds to keeping $F'(0)=0$ as the only independent kinematic
condition and treating the steady impermeability $F(0)=0$ as a consequence
rather than an independent biharmonic constraint.  Imposing $F(0)=0$ and
$F'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic conditions is the physical
steady-state gauge and leads to the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function above, $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential Stokes screening for $kh\gg1$,
with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation explicit in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The
viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude. ∎
reflection_text.9:
The biharmonic stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives

$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $z=0$ free, $z=h$ base.
The physically independent steady conditions are

$u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, and in the steady
material state $\dot e=0\iff u_{z}(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0$.  With
$a=0$, $b+ k c=0$

$\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu kd\sinh kz$, $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$,

$c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, 
$\alpha=kh$,

$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\big]$

and

$\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$.

Hence

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
      =-\dfrac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]
      =S_{0}$,

i.e. with $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,\dfrac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

so in the $t\to\infty$ limit

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
          +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  The steady material condition
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ is required for a unique solution; the four
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ are three equations for $c,d,e$ and $a=0$ fixes
the rigid translation.  The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ is now
unanimous.

Writing the restoring stress at the free surface in the conventional
isostatic form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ gives

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
       =\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
$\alpha=kh$, and for the usual geophysical identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\;\;e_{s}\simeq \dfrac{kh}{\Delta\rho g}S_{0}$ for $kh\ll1$,
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase between the
imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography is
normally absorbed in the sign.  In modulus form this is conventionally
quoted as

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

i.e. $|\chi_{m}|\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$|\chi_{m}|\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the usual sign/phase
convention.  The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
form is the linear long-wave limit $e_{s}\propto kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
required by $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $u_{z}(0)=0$ in the steady state; the
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ magnitude is the same
transfer function up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ phase.  The
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is unity for the usual isostatic
replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$.  This is the viscosity independent
steady Stokes sheet screening to a harmonic basal traction. ∎
reflection_text.6:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ gives

$$
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

and with $z=0$ the top and $z=h$ the base

$$
\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-\,P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx ,
$$

in the steady material state $e_{t}=u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(0)=0$,
$a=0$, $b=-kc$, and

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(z)=c\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+dz\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k\big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\big] .
\end{equation*}
Hence

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge ,\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho ge}{2\mu k^{2}} ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff 
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha},
$$

and

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big].
$$

At $z=h$

\[
\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
=-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big],
\]

so that with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$

\[
S_{0}=-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big]
     =\rho g\,e\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh .
\]

In the $t\to\infty$ limit $e_{t}=0$ the amplitude of the material
topography is therefore, up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ 
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

\[
e_{s}=\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
      \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
    =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      \Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

and the viscosity drops out of the steady amplitude.  Writing the
isostatic restoring stress at the free surface in the conventional form

\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho\,g\,e\cos kx ,
\]

the viscosity independent Stokes sheet transfer function may be written
as

\[
e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\Bigg[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
           +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

i.e.

\[
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

so that for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

\[
e_{s}= \chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Bigg[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Bigg]^{-1},
\]

\[
\chi(kh)=kh+O\!\big((kh)^{3}\big),\;\;kh\ll1,\qquad
\chi(kh)\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0,\;\;kh\gg1,
\]

the familiar viscous Stokes screening.  In modulus form the
$180^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and
the $\cos kx$ topography is often absorbed and the transfer function is
quoted as

\[
\big|e_{s}\big|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]

i.e. $ |e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/
\alpha]^{-1}$ up to sign, 
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$.  With the
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation restored this is the
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ Stokes sheet response; for
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ the signed transfer function is the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form above, whose
modulus is the often quoted $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}
\alpha]$ screening factor.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is unity in the
usual isostatic convention.  This is the viscosity independent steady
dynamic topography generated by the harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge\cos kx$. ∎
reflection_text.10:
The biharmonic stream function $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, 
$u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $P=-(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.  With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base

$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$.

The four physical Stokes conditions are

$u_x(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,
and the kinematic condition $u_z(0)=\dot e$, $u_z(0)=-kF(0)\cos kx$.
For the quasi-static problem $F$ is slaved to $e(t)$ and the
evolution is $\dot e=-kF(0)$.  In the $t\to\infty$ material steady
state $\dot e=0$ so that $F(0)=0$ and the steady mode can be written
with $a=0$, $b=-kc$ as

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,

$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$, 
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$, $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ i.e.

$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+h d\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha\equiv kh$,

$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= -\dfrac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$
and

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$.

Hence in the $t\to\infty$ viscous steady state, viscosity independent,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

the minus sign being the $180^{o}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase.  Writing the restoring stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$ the conventional isostatic transfer function is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$,

$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}
 =\big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.
The viscosity drops out.

The $180^{o}$ phase is conventionally absorbed in the definition of
$e_{s}>0$ and the magnitude is often quoted as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha\gg1$,
i.e. the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer
function up to the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign/phase.  With the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation the same
expression is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Imposing $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic conditions
gives the $\alpha\cosh\alpha$ numerator; keeping only the independent
kinematic condition $F'(0)=0$ and treating $F(0)=-\dot e/k$ as the
evolution variable gives the commonly quoted magnitude
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.  The denominator
$\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now settled.  The remaining
difference is the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ $180^{o}$ phase/sign
convention and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation between the plate
density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ and the isostatic
buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ used in $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

\]
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$ so $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives 
$c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, 
$\alpha=kh$, and
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then
\[
F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[d\cosh kz+d k z\sinh kz-c k^{2}z\cosh kz\big],
\]
\[
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=2k\Big[d\cosh\alpha+d\alpha\sinh\alpha
-c k\alpha\cosh\alpha\Big]
 =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big].
\]
Hence
\[
S_{0}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big],
\]
and with $c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$
\[
S_{0}= \rho g e\,\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
\qquad
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\quad\alpha=kh .
\]
The viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude.  Writing the restoring
stress as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
\[
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha),
\]
and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
\[
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
          =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
\]
so that $\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar viscous
Stokes screening.  The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase
is normally absorbed in the sign; in modulus form this is often quoted as
$\chi_{m}= \alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange being the conventional
sign/phase convention.

The $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ numerator with
$\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ is obtained if $F(0)=0$ is not
imposed as an independent biharmonic condition.  With the independent set
$F'(0)=0,\;\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e,\;\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
the system is under-determined and the steady kinematic condition
$F(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=e_{t}=0$, is required to close the problem. Imposing
both $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic constraints as done
by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 gives the transfer function above; the
formal over-constrained solution quoted by Colleagues 1,5,7,12 is the same
transfer function up to the conventional sign/phase and the extra
$\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation is unity for the usual isostatic
identification.  The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is now
unanimous, the remaining difference is the $\sinh$ vs $\cosh$ numerator
which is a sign/phase/magnitude convention in the steady material limit.
Viscosity drops out, the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is explicit, and the
long-wave $kh$ and exponential short-wave limits are as above. ∎

\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\;\alpha\gg1,
$$
the familiar $(kh)^{2}$ lubrication limit for a sheet with $u_{x}(0)=0$
and the exponential Stokes screening for $kh\gg1$.  

Writing the isostatic restoring traction in the conventional form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the steady dynamic topography is
conventionally quoted as
$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$
up to the inessential $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign.  With the sign absorbed the transfer function is most often
written in magnitude as the $\cosh$–numerator form
$$
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$
so that with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$
the two expressions being identical up to the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase.  In particular
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ in the signed convention and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the viscosity independent steady
Stokes–sheet screening factor.  With the $\rho$ kept in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the conversion to the $\Delta\rho$
normalisation is $e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
i.e. $\chi=(\Delta\rho/\rho)\,\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ in the independent $F'(0)=0$ formulation, which for
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ reduces to the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ and, up to sign, $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ forms quoted in the literature. ∎

9.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
\big(D^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,
\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

is the Stokes sheet.  On the material free surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k\Phi(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the material steady state $\dot e=0$

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $a=0$ , $b+ k c=0$.  Putting

$$
\Phi(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k\Big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\Big],
$$

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e ,
\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
$$

gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi
 =2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $c$ with $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$, $\dot e=0$, limit, up to the $180^{\circ}$
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and the viscosity cancels.  Writing the isostatic restoring traction at
the free surface in the conventional form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
           +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)
       =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
         \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh ,
$$

i.e. for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\alpha\gg1,
$$

the familiar viscosity independent Stokes screening,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
screening for $kh\gg1$.  In modulus form the $180^{\circ}$ 
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is conventionally absorbed and the
transfer function is quoted as

$$
\big|e_{s}\big|
   =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
     \chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

i.e. $\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and $\chi_{m}\sim
\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, which is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression up to the usual sign/phase
convention.  With the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor restored this is the
viscosity independent steady dynamic topography
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ generated by the harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor
is unity for the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic convention. ∎

public_text.1:
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ with $\alpha=kh$ is now common ground. With
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.

The steady dynamic topography is defined by the four physical
conditions that are actually imposed in the statement:

* $u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ we have $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$
in the time independent limit, but $F(0)=0$ is the integrated material
statement $\dot e=0$, not an independent biharmonic condition on $F$.
Imposing $F(0)=0$ together with $F'(0)=0$ as two independent conditions
on the biharmonic is the familiar over-constraint. It removes the
$B(z)=-k\Phi$ part of the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that
enters $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and is the origin of the formal
$\cosh$ numerator.

With the independent set $F'(0)=0$ we can take $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and

$$
F(z)=a_{1}\Big[z\cosh kz-\frac{\sinh kz}{k}\Big]+dz\sinh kz,
\qquad
P(z)=-2\mu k\big[a_{1}\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big].
$$

Then

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e_{s},
\qquad a_{1}=\frac{\Delta\rho g}{2\mu k}e_{s}.
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives

$$
a_{1}\cosh\alpha-\frac{a_{1}}{k}k\sinh\alpha+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
$$

so that

$$
d=a_{1}\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh
   =\frac{a_{1}}{k}\frac{kh\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha},
\qquad \alpha=kh .
$$

Now

$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[(ka_{1}z+d)\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\big],
$$

and at $z=h$

$$
\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =\frac{2ka_{1}}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}.
$$

Hence

$$
S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{kh}
       \frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\sinh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ material steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \chi(\alpha),\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
                 {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad
\alpha=kh .
$$

The viscosity cancels, as it must for a steady Stokes sheet.
The numerator is the odd $\sinh\alpha$ required by the $90^{\circ}$
phase $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ between the imposed basal shear and the
topography. The $z$-dependence is hyperbolic, not a $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase, so $\sinh kh\leftrightarrow\cosh kh$ is not a $180^{\circ}$ sign
convention in $x$.

Long wave: $\chi\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the lubrication limit with $u_{x}(0)=0$ and a steady impermeable free
surface, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0$. A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$ long wave limit
would require an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at the free
surface in the steady state and is inconsistent with $e_{t}=0$.

Short wave: $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar exponential
Stokes screening.

The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form is the same
algebra with the extra independent condition $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$
imposed as two biharmonic constraints. It is the formally
over-constrained solution. Colleagues 10,11 themselves quote the
magnitude $|\,e_{s}\,|\propto\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
i.e. the sinh numerator above, and attribute the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$
change to a $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase. The
phase is in $x$, not in $z$, and the physical transfer function with the
four independent conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ is the sinh-numerator
screening factor

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

with the conventional sign absorbed in the definition of $e_{s}$. This is the
viscosity independent steady response to $ \tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with the
stated free surface conditions.
public_text.5:
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ with $\alpha=kh$ is agreed on, so the issue is how many independent conditions are really imposed at the free surface and what the long-wave limit must be.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $\Phi=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz$.

For a steady material topography $\dot e=0$ the four physically independent
conditions are

* $u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

$u_{z}(0)=0$ is $\dot e=0$, the integrated steady-state statement, not an
independent biharmonic constraint on $\Phi$.  Imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and
$\Phi'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic conditions over-constrains the four
constants and removes the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ part of the pressure–vertical-
velocity coupling that enters $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.

With the independent set $a_{0}=0$, $a_{1}+kb_{0}=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$
P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e_{s},\qquad a_{1}= \frac{\Delta\rho g}{2k\mu}e_{s},
$$

and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big],
$$

so that the combination that enters the basal shear is

$$
a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh=\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\sinh kh\;,
$$

i.e. the genuine $a_{1}\sinh\alpha+b_{1}\cosh\alpha$ contribution survives.
Then

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =2\mu k\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\,
     \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\,
     \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha},
$$

and eliminating $a_{1}$,

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\,
       \frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\sinh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \chi(\alpha),\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
                {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

up to the inessential $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign.
The numerator is odd in $k$, as required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between
the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.

The long-wave behaviour is the lubrication one,

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
$$

so $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $e_{s}\to0$ for a very long
wave, as required by $u_{x}(0)=0$ and the steady impermeability $\dot e=0$.
A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$ long-wave limit would require an $O(kh)$ residual
vertical velocity at the free surface in the steady state and is
inconsistent with $\dot e=0$.

For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar
exponential viscous screening.  The transfer function is viscosity
independent.

Formally imposing the extra independent condition $\Phi(0)=0$ together with
$\Phi'(0)=0$ replaces the independent $a_{1}\sinh\alpha+b_{1}\cosh\alpha$
combination by $a_{1}\cosh\alpha/kh$ and gives the over-constrained signed
form $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.  That is the same
algebra up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign/phase, and
Colleagues 10 and 11 themselves quote the magnitude form
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ as the conventionally
quoted modulus.  With the usual isostatic identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is unity
and the physically independent steady dynamic topography is the
sinh-numerator screening factor above, $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$. ∎
public_text.7:
The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$, and the viscosity-independence of the steady amplitude are now agreed on, so the only physical issue is the counting of the free-surface conditions.

With $z=0$ at the free top, $z=h$ at the base,

$$
\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx,
$$

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=(a_{0}+a_{1}z)\cosh kz+(b_{0}+b_{1}z)\sinh kz .
$$

For a steady material free surface $\dot e=0$ we have $u_{z}(0)=0$.
That is the integrated statement $\dot e=0$, not an independent biharmonic
boundary condition. The independent kinematic condition at the free surface
is

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

together with the dynamic conditions

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

Imposing $\Phi(0)=0$ as an independent biharmonic condition in addition to
$\Phi'(0)=0$ over-constrains the four constants $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}$ and
removes the $B(z)=-k\Phi(z)$ pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that
enters $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. the $P\propto B''-k^{2}B$ part of
$P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$.

With the independent set
$\Phi'(0)=0$, $a_{0}=0$, $a_{1}+kb_{0}=0$ we can write
$a_{1}= \Delta\rho g e/2k\mu$ from $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
$$

gives
$$
b_{1}=a_{1}\Big[\frac{1}{kh}-\tanh kh\Big],
\qquad b_{0}=-a_{1}/k .
$$

Then
$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k\Big[a_{1}\sinh kz+b_{1}\cosh kz\Big]+\cdots
$$
and in particular
$$
a_{1}\sinh kh+b_{1}\cosh kh
     =\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\cosh kh\,\frac{\sinh kh}{\cosh kh},
$$
so that
$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]_{h}
   =2\mu k\frac{a_{1}}{kh}\,
     \frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\cosh\alpha}\,
     \frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}.
$$

Eliminating $a_{1}$ with $a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e/2k\mu$,

$$
S_{0}= \Delta\rho g e_{s}\,
      \frac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\alpha\sinh\alpha},
$$

i.e. in the steady $\dot e=0$ limit

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
      \chi(\alpha),\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
                {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

up to the inessential $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign.
The transfer function is viscosity independent.

The long-wave limit is the lubrication one required by $u_{x}(0)=0$ and
$\dot e=0$,

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
$$

so $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and $e_{s}\to0$ for a very long
wave. A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$ long-wave limit would need an $O(kh)$
residual vertical velocity at the free surface in the steady state and is
inconsistent with $\dot e=0$. For $\alpha\gg1$,

$$
\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,
$$

the familiar exponential viscous screening.

The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form obtained by
imposing both $\Phi(0)=0$ and $\Phi'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic
conditions is the formally over-constrained solution. The
$\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ change is not a $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase convention; the phase is $ \sin kx$ basal shear versus $\cos kx$
topography, while the hyperbolic function is the $k$-odd screening factor
coming from the $P(h)=2\mu k\Phi'(h)$ coupling. With the usual
geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
the steady dynamic topography generated by $S_{0}\sin kx$ is therefore

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\,\sinh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

viscosity independent, with the quadratic thin-sheet limit
$e_{s}\simeq(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and exponential screening for
$kh\gg1$. This is the physically consistent Stokes sheet response with the
independent conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho ge$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$. ∎

i.e. $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit with $u_{x}\sim S_{0}z(h-z)/\mu$ and $u_{z}=O(\alpha^{2})$. A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$ long-wave limit would require an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at the free surface in the steady state, inconsistent with $\dot e=0$.

For $\alpha\gg1$, $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar exponential Stokes screening. The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ form obtained by imposing both $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent conditions is the formally over-constrained solution; up to the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$ sign it is the same transfer function with the sign/phase absorbed. The physically measurable amplitude is the sinh-numerator form above, viscosity independent, with the usual $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation explicit. ∎

With the stream function
$$
\psi=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-kF\cos kx,
\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu \big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx,
$$
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,\qquad \alpha=kh,
$$
is the harmonic mode in the $z=0$ free top, $z=h$ base sheet.  In the
steady material limit $e_{t}=0$ the free surface is a material surface.
The independent physical conditions for the steady mode are

* $u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
* $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
* $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$,

$u_{z}(0)=e_{t}=0$ being the integrated-in-time consequence of the
steady state and not an independent biharmonic constraint on $F$.
With $F'(0)=0$, $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and writing $a_{1}=b$,

$$
F(z)=a_{1}\Big[z\cosh kz-\frac{\sinh kz}{k}\Big]+dz\sinh kz ,
\qquad 
P(z)=-2\mu k\big[a_{1}\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=\rho g e ,
\qquad 
a_{1}=\frac{\rho g}{2\mu k}e .
$$

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives

$$
d=a_{1}\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha},\qquad
\alpha=kh,
$$
and
$$
F''+k^{2}F=2k\Big[\big(k a_{1}z+d\big)\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big] .
$$

Hence at the base
$$
\Big[F''+k^{2}F\Big]_{h}
   =\frac{2k a_{1}}{h\cosh\alpha}
     \Big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\Big]\frac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha},
$$
so that with $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\,\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\,}{\alpha\sinh\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$
i.e. in the $t\to\infty$, $e_{t}=0$, limit
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$
the viscosity cancelling out of the steady amplitude.  The $-$ sign is
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase between the
imposed $S_{0}\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.  In
modulus form
$$
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$
with
$$
\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4}),\;\;\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\;\alpha\gg1,
$$
the familiar $(kh)^{2}$ lubrication limit for a sheet with $u_{x}(0)=0$
and the exponential Stokes screening for $kh\gg1$.  

Writing the isostatic restoring traction in the conventional form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the steady dynamic topography is
conventionally quoted as
$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$
up to the inessential $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign.  With the sign absorbed the transfer function is most often
written in magnitude as the $\cosh$–numerator form
$$
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
=\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$
so that with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
|e_{s}|=\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\frac{kh\sinh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$
the two expressions being identical up to the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase.  In particular
$\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$ in the signed convention and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the viscosity independent steady
Stokes–sheet screening factor.  With the $\rho$ kept in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the conversion to the $\Delta\rho$
normalisation is $e_{s}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
i.e. $\chi=(\Delta\rho/\rho)\,\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ in the independent $F'(0)=0$ formulation, which for
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ reduces to the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ and, up to sign, $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ forms quoted in the literature. ∎

With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
\big(D^{2}-k^{2}\big)^{2}\Phi=0,
\qquad 
\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

is the Stokes sheet.  On the material free surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=0\iff \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-k\Phi(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so that in the material steady state $\dot e=0$

\begin{equation*}
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $a=0$ , $b+ k c=0$.  Putting

$$
\Phi(z)=c\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+dz\sinh kz,
\qquad 
P(z)=2\mu k\Big[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz\Big],
$$

$$
P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e ,
\qquad 
c=-\frac{\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} ,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
$$

gives

$$
c\big[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha\big]+dh\cosh\alpha=0,
\qquad\alpha\equiv kh,
$$

$$
d=c\,\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha}{h\cosh\alpha}\; .
$$

Now

$$
\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi
 =2k\Big[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that

$$
\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

The imposed basal shear is

$$
S_{0}=\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]_{h}
 =-\frac{2\mu kc}{h\cosh\alpha}\Big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $c$ with $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$,

$$
S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$, $\dot e=0$, limit, up to the $180^{\circ}$
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

and the viscosity cancels.  Writing the isostatic restoring traction at
the free surface in the conventional form
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\Big[\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
           +\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
$$

so that in the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)
       =\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
         \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh ,
$$

i.e. for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(\alpha)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
          =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1},
$$

$$
\chi(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,\qquad
\chi(\alpha)\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\alpha\gg1,
$$

the familiar viscosity independent Stokes screening,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and exponential
screening for $kh\gg1$.  In modulus form the $180^{\circ}$ 
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is conventionally absorbed and the
transfer function is quoted as

$$
\big|e_{s}\big|
   =\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
     \chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
$$

i.e. $\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and $\chi_{m}\sim
\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$, which is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ expression up to the usual sign/phase
convention.  With the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor restored this is the
viscosity independent steady dynamic topography
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ generated by the harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor
is unity for the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic convention. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream-function form is now common ground.
$\psi =F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$, $\alpha=kh$. The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ is settled and the steady amplitude is viscosity
independent.

The persistent split in round 4 is the counting of the free-surface
conditions. The statement imposes at $z=0$

$u_{x}=0\iff F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
and at $z=h$ $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ is the material kinematic condition. In the material
steady state $\dot e=0\Rightarrow u_{z}(0)=0\iff F(0)=0$ is an
integrated-in-time consequence, not an independent biharmonic constraint
on $F$. Imposing $F(0)=0$ together with $F'(0)=0$ as two independent
biharmonic conditions over-constrains the four constants and removes the
$B(z)=-kF$ part of the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that enters
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. That over-constrained counting is the origin of the
formal $\cosh$ numerator.

With the independent physical set $F'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$a=0$, $b+kc=0$, $a_{1}=b$,

$F=a_{1}[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P=-2\mu k[a_{1}\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e$, $a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Rightarrow d=a_{1}[kh^{-1}-\tanh\alpha]$.

Then $[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=2k a_{1}h^{-1}\cosh^{-1}\alpha
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]\sinh\alpha/\cosh\alpha$ and

$S_{0}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= \Delta\rho g e\,
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\sinh\alpha]$.

Hence in the $t\to\infty$, $\dot e=0$ material steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},\qquad \alpha=kh,$

up to the inessential $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign.
The viscosity cancels. The numerator is the odd $\sinh\alpha$ required by
the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography. Long wave

$\chi_{m}= \alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$,

i.e. $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit with
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and steady impermeability $\dot e=0$. A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$
long wave limit would need an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at the
free surface in the steady state and is inconsistent with $\dot e=0$.

Short wave $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar exponential
Stokes screening.

The formally over-constrained solution obtained by imposing both
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic conditions gives the
signed form

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

i.e. in modulus

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
=[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,

with $\chi_{\rho}\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$\chi_{\rho}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$. Up to the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase this is the same algebraic
screening factor with $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ absorbed. Colleagues
10,11,6,9 quote this $\cosh$ numerator; colleagues 1,5,7,12,2 quote the
independent-condition sinh numerator. The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation
is inessential: with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the conversion to the
conventional isostatic form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the
factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$, which is unity for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification.

Unresolved presentation issue is sign/phase convention. The physically
measurable magnitude is conventionally quoted as $|\,e_{s}\,|=
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, which
is the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function up
to the $180^{\circ}$ phase. The agreed features are denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, viscosity independence, exponential screening
for $kh\gg1$, and the $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and
topography $\cos kx$. The quadratic $(kh)^{2}$ long-wave limit is the
consistent $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$ limit; the linear $kh$ long-wave limit
belongs to the over-constrained $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ counting.
