11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic sheet is now settled up to the counting of the free-surface
kinematic condition.  With $\psi =F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, 
$u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $\alpha=kh$.

Denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and viscosity independence of the
steady amplitude are common ground.  The four mechanical data are
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the material coupling
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e$.  In the material steady state $\dot e=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$ is a consequence of the steady state,
$F'(0)=0$ is the independent kinematic condition at the deflected top.
Imposing $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic
constraints is the over-constrained gauge that is often used in the
literature.

With the independent set $F'(0)=0$, $a=0$, $b=-kc$,

$F(z)=a_{1}\!\left[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\right]+dz\sinh kz$, 
$P(z)=-2\mu k[a_{1}\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=\rho g e$, $a_{1}=\rho g e/2\mu k$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$d=a_{1}\big[kh^{-1}-\tanh\alpha\big]$ and

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =\dfrac{2k a_{1}}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]\dfrac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$.

Hence

$S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =\rho g e\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}$,
i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ material steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,$

the minus sign being the conventional $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow
\cos kx$ phase.  Viscosity cancels.  Writing the isostatic restoring
traction in the conventional form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad
\alpha=kh,$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit with
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$, and $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$
for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar exponential Stokes screening.  Up to the
inessential $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase this is the
conventionally quoted signed form

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
   \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e. $\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
$\chi\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for
$\alpha\gg1$, with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation made explicit by
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange is the usual $180^{\circ}$
phase absorption.  The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and the
viscosity independence are settled; the remaining dispute is the
independent counting of $F(0)=0$ versus $F'(0)=0$ and the resulting
$\alpha\sinh\alpha$ versus $\alpha\cosh\alpha$ numerator, i.e. the
$\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ versus $\chi\sim\alpha$ long-wave limit. ∎

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes sheet is  
$\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$.

With $z=0$ free top, $z=h$ base the four mechanical data are
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In the material steady state $\dot e=0$ gives $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(0)=0$ as a consequence of the evolution.  With
$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ the $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$
conditions give $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$\Phi(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$,

$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ gives
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha=kh$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz]$ and

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Hence
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

i.e. up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  Writing the isostatic restoring traction as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,

and in the normalisation $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$
for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,
$\alpha=kh$.

In particular
$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $kh\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar exponential Stokes
screening.

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is conventionally
absorbed in the modulus.  The modulus is often quoted as

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

i.e. $|\chi_{m}|\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$|\chi_{m}|\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ signed form and the
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ magnitude form are the
same transfer function up to the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign/phase.  The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ with
$\alpha=kh$ and the viscosity independence of the steady amplitude are
now common ground.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is unity for the usual
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic identification.  The long-wave
$\chi\sim\alpha$ signed, $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha^{2}$ magnitude, and the
short-wave exponential decay $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ are the
physically consistent Stokes-sheet screening to a harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎

     +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress written in
the conventional form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the
normalised form is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.
The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign is conventionally
absorbed, $ |e_{s}|$ being quoted with the modulus
$\chi_{m}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is settled and the viscosity
cancels in the steady amplitude.  The $\sinh$-numerator forms appearing in
the literature are the same transfer function up to the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase / sign and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$
normalisation between the plate density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
and the isostatic buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ used in $e_{s}=\chi
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The over-constrained $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ counting is the
source of the $\cosh$-versus-$\sinh$ nomenclature; with the four physical
Stokes conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and the steady kinematics $F(0)=0$ the cosh-numerator
screening factor above is the viscosity independent steady Stokes-sheet
response. ∎

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic sheet with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $\Phi=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$ is now settled.
Denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$, and viscosity
independence of the steady amplitude are common ground.

The four mechanical data are $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
The material condition is $u_{z}(0)=\dot e$, i.e. $-k\Phi(0)=\dot e$.
In the material steady limit $\dot e=0$ the biharmonic constants close
with $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $a=0$, $b=-kc$,
$\Phi(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu k d\sinh kz$.
Then $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$.
Hence
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2kc h^{-1}(\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha)
\cosh^{-1}\alpha$ and
$S_{0}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
      =\rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$.
The steady material amplitude is therefore, up to the
$180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity cancels.  With the isostatic restoring traction
written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $180^{\circ}$ phase is conventionally absorbed in the modulus,
$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
so that in magnitude
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $\sinh$ numerator is the signed $\cosh$ numerator with the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase absorbed.  The $\alpha^{2}$ long-wave
limit quoted by the $F'(0)=0$ only counting is the transient
$\dot e\neq0$ counting in which $\Phi(0)=0$ is not imposed as an
independent biharmonic condition; the steady material limit requires
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ and gives the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ screening factor above, i.e. the familiar
$[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ Stokes sheet response,
up to the inessential sign/phase and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic sheet solution is now essentially settled. With
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$,
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
the mechanical data at $z=0$ free and $z=h$ base are

$u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In the $t\to\infty$ material steady state $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kF(0)=0$ so
that $F(0)=0$ is a consequence of the steady state.  With 
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$,

$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, 
$\alpha=kh$,

$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$F''+k^{2}F=2k[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz]$ and

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=-2kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Hence

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$
$\iff S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

i.e. up to the $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
 \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
 \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  Writing the isostatic restoring traction as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional normalisation is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
       =\big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.  The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and the viscosity independence are agreed on.

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is conventionally
absorbed in the magnitude.  In modulus form the transfer function is
often quoted as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$
for $\alpha\gg1$, which is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
expression with the sign/phase absorbed.  The sinh numerator is the
$k$–odd form required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography and is the form obtained
if $F(0)=0$ is treated as the integrated steady-state consequence
$\dot e=0$ and not as an independent biharmonic constraint.  Imposing
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic conditions gives the
signed $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ screening factor
above, the two forms differing only by the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase/sign.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is explicit; for
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ it is unity. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes mode can be written with
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$ and

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
With $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ the four mechanical
data are $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ and the material
steady state is $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$.  Up to the
additive constant $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$,

$c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]
+hd\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha=kh$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=-2kc[h\cosh\alpha]^{-1}
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$

and

$S_{0}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}
     =\rho ge\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$.

In the $t\to\infty$, $\dot e=0$, material steady state, up to the
conventional $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,$

and the viscosity cancels.  With the isostatic restoring traction
written in the conventional form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the transfer function is

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\Delta\rho/\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
$\alpha=kh$,

so that for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
        =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq kh+O((kh)^{3})$, $kh\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, $kh\gg1$, 
i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for long waves and the
familiar exponential Stokes screening for short waves.  In modulus
form the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase is absorbed and the
transfer function is conventionally quoted as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha\gg1$,

which is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
expression up to the usual sign/phase convention.  The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and the viscosity independence are now
unanimous; the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ numerator is the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor is unity for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ and is explicit otherwise.
This is the stable, viscosity independent Stokes sheet response
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ to the harmonic basal shear
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎

reflection_text.2:
The biharmonic stream-function form is now common ground.
$\psi =F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$, $\alpha=kh$. The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ is settled and the steady amplitude is viscosity
independent.

The persistent split in round 4 is the counting of the free-surface
conditions. The statement imposes at $z=0$

$u_{x}=0\iff F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
and at $z=h$ $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e$ is the material kinematic condition. In the material
steady state $\dot e=0\Rightarrow u_{z}(0)=0\iff F(0)=0$ is an
integrated-in-time consequence, not an independent biharmonic constraint
on $F$. Imposing $F(0)=0$ together with $F'(0)=0$ as two independent
biharmonic conditions over-constrains the four constants and removes the
$B(z)=-kF$ part of the pressure–vertical-velocity coupling that enters
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. That over-constrained counting is the origin of the
formal $\cosh$ numerator.

With the independent physical set $F'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$a=0$, $b+kc=0$, $a_{1}=b$,

$F=a_{1}[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P=-2\mu k[a_{1}\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e$, $a_{1}=\Delta\rho g e/2\mu k$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Rightarrow d=a_{1}[kh^{-1}-\tanh\alpha]$.

Then $[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=2k a_{1}h^{-1}\cosh^{-1}\alpha
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]\sinh\alpha/\cosh\alpha$ and

$S_{0}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}= \Delta\rho g e\,
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\sinh\alpha]$.

Hence in the $t\to\infty$, $\dot e=0$ material steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha),\qquad 
\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},\qquad \alpha=kh,$

up to the inessential $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign.
The viscosity cancels. The numerator is the odd $\sinh\alpha$ required by
the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear and the
$\cos kx$ topography. Long wave

$\chi_{m}= \alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$, $\alpha\ll1$,

i.e. $e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit with
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and steady impermeability $\dot e=0$. A linear $\chi\sim\alpha$
long wave limit would need an $O(\alpha)$ residual vertical velocity at the
free surface in the steady state and is inconsistent with $\dot e=0$.

Short wave $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, the familiar exponential
Stokes screening.

The formally over-constrained solution obtained by imposing both
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as independent biharmonic conditions gives the
signed form

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

i.e. in modulus

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
=[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$,

with $\chi_{\rho}\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$\chi_{\rho}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$. Up to the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase this is the same algebraic
screening factor with $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ absorbed. Colleagues
10,11,6,9 quote this $\cosh$ numerator; colleagues 1,5,7,12,2 quote the
independent-condition sinh numerator. The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation
is inessential: with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the conversion to the
conventional isostatic form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the
factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$, which is unity for the usual $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
identification.

Unresolved presentation issue is sign/phase convention. The physically
measurable magnitude is conventionally quoted as $|\,e_{s}\,|=
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, which
is the $\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ transfer function up
to the $180^{\circ}$ phase. The agreed features are denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, viscosity independence, exponential screening
for $kh\gg1$, and the $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and
topography $\cos kx$. The quadratic $(kh)^{2}$ long-wave limit is the
consistent $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$ limit; the linear $kh$ long-wave limit
belongs to the over-constrained $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ counting.

reflection_text.11:
The biharmonic sheet is now settled up to the counting of the free-surface
kinematic condition.  With $\psi =F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, 
$u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $\alpha=kh$.

Denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and viscosity independence of the
steady amplitude are common ground.  The four mechanical data are
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the material coupling
$u_{z}(0)=\dot e$.  In the material steady state $\dot e=0$,
$u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$ is a consequence of the steady state,
$F'(0)=0$ is the independent kinematic condition at the deflected top.
Imposing $F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic
constraints is the over-constrained gauge that is often used in the
literature.

With the independent set $F'(0)=0$, $a=0$, $b=-kc$,

$F(z)=a_{1}\!\left[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\right]+dz\sinh kz$, 
$P(z)=-2\mu k[a_{1}\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k a_{1}=\rho g e$, $a_{1}=\rho g e/2\mu k$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$d=a_{1}\big[kh^{-1}-\tanh\alpha\big]$ and

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
 =\dfrac{2k a_{1}}{h\cosh\alpha}
   \big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]\dfrac{\sinh\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}$.

Hence

$S_{0}=\mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}
     =\rho g e\,\dfrac{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}{\alpha\sinh\alpha}$,
i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ material steady state

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha},
\qquad\alpha=kh,$

the minus sign being the conventional $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow
\cos kx$ phase.  Viscosity cancels.  Writing the isostatic restoring
traction in the conventional form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},\qquad
\alpha=kh,$

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}+O(\alpha^{4})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$e_{s}\propto(kh)^{2}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the lubrication limit with
$u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\dot e=0$, and $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$
for $\alpha\gg1$, the familiar exponential Stokes screening.  Up to the
inessential $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase this is the
conventionally quoted signed form

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
   \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,

i.e. $\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
$\chi\simeq\alpha$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for
$\alpha\gg1$, with the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation made explicit by
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ versus $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ interchange is the usual $180^{\circ}$
phase absorption.  The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and the
viscosity independence are settled; the remaining dispute is the
independent counting of $F(0)=0$ versus $F'(0)=0$ and the resulting
$\alpha\sinh\alpha$ versus $\alpha\cosh\alpha$ numerator, i.e. the
$\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ versus $\chi\sim\alpha$ long-wave limit. ∎
reflection_text.9:
The harmonic Stokes sheet is  
$\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$.

With $z=0$ free top, $z=h$ base the four mechanical data are
$u_{x}(0)=0\iff\Phi'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, 
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
In the material steady state $\dot e=0$ gives $u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(0)=0$ as a consequence of the evolution.  With
$\Phi(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ the $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\Phi(0)=0$
conditions give $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$\Phi(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$,

$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ gives
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha=kh$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then
$\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi=2k[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz]$ and

$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=-2kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Hence
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

i.e. up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  Writing the isostatic restoring traction as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,

and in the normalisation $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$
for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,
$\alpha=kh$.

In particular
$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $kh\ll1$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$ for $kh\gg1$, the familiar exponential Stokes
screening.

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is conventionally
absorbed in the modulus.  The modulus is often quoted as

$|e_{s}|=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\sinh\alpha}
{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,

i.e. $|\chi_{m}|\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$|\chi_{m}|\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ signed form and the
$\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ magnitude form are the
same transfer function up to the conventional $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
sign/phase.  The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ with
$\alpha=kh$ and the viscosity independence of the steady amplitude are
now common ground.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is unity for the usual
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ isostatic identification.  The long-wave
$\chi\sim\alpha$ signed, $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha^{2}$ magnitude, and the
short-wave exponential decay $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ are the
physically consistent Stokes-sheet screening to a harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎
reflection_text.6:
The harmonic mode can be written with a stream function

$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.

With $z=0$ free, $z=h$ base,
$F=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.
In the material steady state $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$ so that
$F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ together with $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$F'(0)=0$.
Hence $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e$ gives $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$,
$c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives with $\alpha=kh$

$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c\,[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/[h\cosh\alpha]$.

Then 
$F''+k^{2}F=2k[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz]$ and

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=-2kc\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[h\cosh\alpha]$.

With $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$

$S_{0}=-\,2\mu kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[h\cosh\alpha]
      =\rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$.

Hence up to the conventional $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
        \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
      =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
        \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
             +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

the viscosity cancels in the steady amplitude.  Writing the isostatic
restoring traction in the conventional form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)S_{0}/\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
and in the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
             \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

so that for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
        =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq kh+O[(kh)^{3}]$, $kh\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, $kh\gg1$.  

In modulus form the $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is
conventionally absorbed and the transfer function is quoted as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$, $\alpha\ll1$, $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$,
$\alpha\gg1$,

i.e. $|\chi_{m}|$ is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
expression up to sign.  The denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and the
viscosity independence of the steady amplitude are the agreed features.
The $\sinh$ numerator is the same screening factor with the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase absorbed; the $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$
over-constrained counting discussed in round 4 gives the $\alpha\sinh\alpha$
magitude form $e_{s}=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,
\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$, $\chi\sim\alpha^{2}$ for
$kh\ll1$ in the independent $F'(0)=0$ formulation, which is identical to the
$\alpha\cosh\alpha$ signed form up to the usual phase convention. ∎
reflection_text.10:
The biharmonic stream function can be written
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ with $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
With $z=0$ top, $z=h$ base

$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$. 
The instantaneous Stokes data are $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ and the material
kinematics $ \dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kF(0)$.  In the material steady state
$\dot e=0$, hence $F(0)=0$ in addition to $F'(0)=0$.  With $a=0$,
$b+ k c=0$

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$, 
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$, 
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0$ gives
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+h d\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha\equiv kh$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.  
Then

$F''+k^{2}F=2k\big[(d-c k^{2}z)\cosh kz+d k z\sinh kz\big]$ and at
$z=h$

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=-2kc[h\cosh\alpha]^{-1}
\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]$.

Hence $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$ gives with the $c$
above

$S_{0}= \rho g e\,
\frac{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}{\alpha\cosh\alpha}$,

i.e. in the $t\to\infty$ material steady state $\dot e=0$

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
\Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
     +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  With the isostatic restoring stress written in
the conventional form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the
normalised form is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\Big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$.
The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign is conventionally
absorbed, $ |e_{s}|$ being quoted with the modulus
$\chi_{m}=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$.
The denominator $\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}$ is settled and the viscosity
cancels in the steady amplitude.  The $\sinh$-numerator forms appearing in
the literature are the same transfer function up to the conventional
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase / sign and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$
normalisation between the plate density used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
and the isostatic buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ used in $e_{s}=\chi
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The over-constrained $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ counting is the
source of the $\cosh$-versus-$\sinh$ nomenclature; with the four physical
Stokes conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ and the steady kinematics $F(0)=0$ the cosh-numerator
screening factor above is the viscosity independent steady Stokes-sheet
response. ∎
reflection_text.8:
The biharmonic sheet with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$, $\Phi=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$ is now settled.
Denominator $\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$, and viscosity
independence of the steady amplitude are common ground.

The four mechanical data are $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.
The material condition is $u_{z}(0)=\dot e$, i.e. $-k\Phi(0)=\dot e$.
In the material steady limit $\dot e=0$ the biharmonic constants close
with $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$, i.e. $a=0$, $b=-kc$,
$\Phi(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k^{2}c\cosh kz-2\mu k d\sinh kz$.
Then $P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$, $\alpha=kh$.
Hence
$[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}= -2kc h^{-1}(\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha)
\cosh^{-1}\alpha$ and
$S_{0}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]_{h}
      =\rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$.
The steady material amplitude is therefore, up to the
$180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity cancels.  With the isostatic restoring traction
written as $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\,\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$,
$\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $180^{\circ}$ phase is conventionally absorbed in the modulus,
$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\,\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
so that in magnitude
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$ and
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$ for $\alpha\gg1$.
The $\sinh$ numerator is the signed $\cosh$ numerator with the
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase absorbed.  The $\alpha^{2}$ long-wave
limit quoted by the $F'(0)=0$ only counting is the transient
$\dot e\neq0$ counting in which $\Phi(0)=0$ is not imposed as an
independent biharmonic condition; the steady material limit requires
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ and gives the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+
\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ screening factor above, i.e. the familiar
$[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha]^{-1}$ Stokes sheet response,
up to the inessential sign/phase and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ normalisation. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The biharmonic sheet solution is now essentially settled. With
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$,
$F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
the mechanical data at $z=0$ free and $z=h$ base are

$u_{x}(0)=0\iff F'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.

In the $t\to\infty$ material steady state $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=-kF(0)=0$ so
that $F(0)=0$ is a consequence of the steady state.  With 
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$,

$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho g e$, $c=-\rho g e/2\mu k^{2}$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]+dh\cosh\alpha=0$, 
$\alpha=kh$,

$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Then

$F''+k^{2}F=2k[-k^{2}cz\cosh kz+d\cosh kz+dkz\sinh kz]$ and

$\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]_{h}=-2kc[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.

Hence

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=S_{0}$
$\iff S_{0}= \rho g e\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/\alpha\cosh\alpha$,

i.e. up to the $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
 \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
 =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
 \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}+\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$,
$\alpha=kh$,

viscosity independent.  Writing the isostatic restoring traction as
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional normalisation is

$e_{s}= \chi(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,

and for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]
       =\big[\alpha/\cosh\alpha+\cosh\alpha/\alpha\big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq\alpha+O(\alpha^{3})$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and $\chi\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$ for $\alpha\gg1$.  The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and the viscosity independence are agreed on.

The $180^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase is conventionally
absorbed in the magnitude.  In modulus form the transfer function is
often quoted as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}\Delta\rho^{-1}g^{-1}\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,

$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$ for $\alpha\ll1$, $\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$
for $\alpha\gg1$, which is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
expression with the sign/phase absorbed.  The sinh numerator is the
$k$–odd form required by the $90^{\circ}$ phase between the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography and is the form obtained
if $F(0)=0$ is treated as the integrated steady-state consequence
$\dot e=0$ and not as an independent biharmonic constraint.  Imposing
$F(0)=0$ and $F'(0)=0$ as two independent biharmonic conditions gives the
signed $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$ screening factor
above, the two forms differing only by the conventional $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase/sign.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$ prefactor is explicit; for
$\rho=\Delta\rho$ it is unity. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The Stokes mode can be written with
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-kF\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$ and

$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$, 
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu kF']\cos kx$.
With $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ the four mechanical
data are $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ and the material
steady state is $\dot e=u_{z}(0)=0$, i.e. $F(0)=0$.  Up to the
additive constant $a=0$, $b=-kc$ and

$F(z)=c[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+dz\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu k[kc\cosh kz-d\sinh kz]$,
$P(0)=2\mu k^{2}c=-\rho ge$,

$c=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff c[\cosh\alpha-\alpha\sinh\alpha]
+hd\cosh\alpha=0$, $\alpha=kh$,
$d=c[\alpha\sinh\alpha-\cosh\alpha]/h\cosh\alpha$.
Then

$[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}=-2kc[h\cosh\alpha]^{-1}
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$

and

$S_{0}=\mu[F''+k^{2}F]_{h}
     =\rho ge\,[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]/[\alpha\cosh\alpha]$.

In the $t\to\infty$, $\dot e=0$, material steady state, up to the
conventional $180^{\circ}\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase,

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha}
     =\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       \Big[\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
            +\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,$

and the viscosity cancels.  With the isostatic restoring traction
written in the conventional form $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
the transfer function is

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(\alpha)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi(\alpha)=(\Delta\rho/\rho)\chi_{\rho}(\alpha)$,
$\alpha=kh$,

so that for the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
        =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi\simeq kh+O((kh)^{3})$, $kh\ll1$, 
$\chi\sim kh\,e^{-kh}\to0$, $kh\gg1$, 
i.e. $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for long waves and the
familiar exponential Stokes screening for short waves.  In modulus
form the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase is absorbed and the
transfer function is conventionally quoted as

$|e_{s}|=S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\;
\chi_{m}(\alpha)$,
$\chi_{m}(\alpha)=\alpha\sinh\alpha/
[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$,
$\chi_{m}\simeq\alpha^{2}$, $\alpha\ll1$, 
$\chi_{m}\sim\alpha e^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha\gg1$,

which is the $\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha]$
expression up to the usual sign/phase convention.  The denominator
$\alpha^{2}+\cosh^{2}\alpha$ and the viscosity independence are now
unanimous; the $\sinh\leftrightarrow\cosh$ numerator is the usual
$\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ sign/phase.  The $\rho/\Delta\rho$
prefactor is unity for $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ and is explicit otherwise.
This is the stable, viscosity independent Stokes sheet response
$e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ to the harmonic basal shear
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ with $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎
